title.en: Australia news live: KMPG axes hundreds of staff in wake of audit leaks scandal; jobseeker now barely two-thirds of pension
title.zh: 澳大利亚新闻直播：毕马威因审计泄密丑闻裁员数百人；求职者津贴仅为养老金的三分之二

summary.en: KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and approximately 360 employees following an audit leaks scandal that resulted in the loss of new government contracts. The consulting giant reported a 1% year-on-year revenue fall, with its consulting arm experiencing a 16.9% decline.
summary.zh: 毕马威澳大利亚公司因审计泄密丑闻导致失去新的政府合同，正在裁减27名合伙人及约360名员工。这家咨询巨头报告称，其收入同比下降1%，其中咨询业务收入下降16.9%。

body.en:
KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and about 360 employees in the wake of an audit leaks scandal that saw it cut off from new government contracts.

The audit and consulting giant today reported its revenue fell 1% year-on-year, to $2.26bn in the year 2025-26.

While the embattled audit arm had seen revenue grow 11%, its consulting revenue was down 16.9%. Most of the workers to be let go are from the consulting arm.

KPMG’s new chief executive, John Sams , said weak demand for its services was expected to continue beyond the next 12 months, blaming Australia’s weak economy. He said:

The professional services sector is also changing rapidly as client expectations evolve, AI reshapes the way services are delivered and government spending on consultants remains lower. We also recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust …

After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to reduce our workforce and restructure parts of the firm. This is not a decision that has been taken lightly, and we know it will have a very real impact on people.

The firm said it was discussing further cuts to a small number of award-based jobs. Sams said KPMG would continue to assess its operating environment as it sought to stay financially sustainable. You can read about the firm’s difficulties here:
body.zh: 毕马威澳大利亚公司在审计泄密丑闻导致其与新政府合同被切断后，正在裁员 27 名合伙人以及约 360 名员工。 这家审计和咨询巨头今天报告称，其 2025-26 年收入同比下降 1%，至 22.6 亿美元。 尽管陷入困境的审计部门收入增长了 11%，但其咨询收入却下降了 16.9%。大多数被解雇的员工来自咨询部门。 毕马威 (KPMG) 新任首席执行官约翰·萨姆斯 (John Sams) 表示，对其服务的疲软需求预计将在未来 12 个月之后持续，并将其归咎于澳大利亚经济疲软。他说： 随着客户期望的变化、人工智能重塑服务提供方式以及政府在顾问方面的支出仍然较低，专业服务行业也在迅速变化。我们还认识到我们自己的失败所带来的挑战，以及我们必须继续努力重建信任...... 经过深思熟虑，我们做出了裁员和重组公司部分部门的艰难决定。这不是一个轻易做出的决定，我们知道这将对人们产生非常现实的影响。 该公司表示正在讨论进一步削减少量奖励职位。萨姆斯表示，毕马威将继续评估其运营环境，以保持财务可持续性。您可以在这里了解该公司的困难：

reflection.en: The news of KPMG Australia cutting hundreds of staff in the wake of an audit leaks scandal reminds us that integrity in professional life has far-reaching consequences. Even seemingly small breaches of trust, like those implied by the "audit leaks," can erode confidence, lead to lost contracts, and ultimately impact the livelihoods of many employees. Yahweh...
reflection.zh: 毕马威澳大利亚公司因审计泄密丑闻裁员数百人的消息提醒我们，职业生涯中的诚信会带来深远的影响。即使是像“审计泄密”这样看似微小的信任破裂，也可能侵蚀信心，导致合同流失，并最终影响许多员工的生计。雅伟呼召我们在所有事务上都忠心耿耿，认识到我们的行为，无论是在“很小的事上”还是“在大事上”，都对我们的社区和工作场所的福祉有所贡献。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

title.en: Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
title.zh: 澳大利亚鲨鱼袭击受害者感谢“第二次生命机会”

summary.en: Leah Stewart was mauled by a shark in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 35, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; £289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.
body.zh: 今年早些时候，一名在悉尼热门海滩被鲨鱼咬伤的澳大利亚妇女表示，她获得了“生命的第二次机会”，并将充分利用它。 6 月，35 岁的莉亚·斯图尔特 (Leah Stewart) 在库吉海滩 (Coogee Beach) 晨泳时被鲨鱼咬伤，手臂和腿部多处被咬伤，澳大利亚发生了一系列袭击事件。 这位一个孩子的母亲陷入昏迷，并接受了多次手术，包括截肢了她的一只手臂。 在周一的一篇在线帖子中，她感谢为她筹集了超过 550,000 澳元（394,000 美元；289,000 英镑）的支持者，并表示她的康复“极其困难”，但她正在取得“显着”进展。 斯图尔特在袭击发生后的第一条评论中写道：“经历了极其困难的几个月后，我很高兴我已经取得了足够的进步，能够建立一些独立性，在这一切之后我终于能看到一些曙光。” “我想让你知道，我觉得我得到了第二次生命机会，我不会浪费它。” 斯图尔特说，家人、朋友和“甚至陌生人”的支持让她“不知所措”，并补充说“你们激励我变得更好，而不是痛苦”。 她写道，为她举办的在线筹款活动现已结束，筹集到的资金让她有机会在家康复，并“为今后进一步的医疗提供选择”。 “我还有很长的路要走，但我的康复非常显着，其中很大一部分原因是来自世界各地围绕着我和我的家人的绝对的爱、支持、祈祷和鼓励。” 今年澳大利亚发生了多起鲨鱼袭击事件，1月份的两天内发生了四起鲨鱼袭击事件，其中一起袭击事件是一名12岁男孩，后来因伤重死亡。 今年 5 月，昆士兰州一名男子在鱼叉捕鱼时被鲨鱼杀死，而在西澳大利亚州，一名两个孩子的父亲被一条 4 米（13 英尺）长的鲨鱼袭击后死亡。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: UK productivity growing faster than official figures suggest, thinktank finds
title.zh: 智库发现：英国生产力增长快于官方数据

summary.en: A thinktank, the Resolution Foundation, reports that UK productivity is growing more strongly than official figures indicate, suggesting the economy may finally be recovering from the impact of the 2008 global financial crisis.
summary.zh: 智库“决议基金会”报告称，英国的生产力增长速度快于官方数据所示，这表明英国经济可能终于从2008年全球金融危机的长期影响中复苏。

body.en: Resolution Foundation suggests economy may finally be emerging from shadow of 2008 financial crisis Productivity in the UK – a vital measure of economic health – is growing more strongly than official figures suggest, according to analysis from the Resolution Foundation. The thinktank suggests the chancellor, John Healey, may have inherited an economy finally starting to emerge from the long shadow of the 2008 global financial crisis. Continue reading...
body.zh: 决议基金会表示，经济可能最终摆脱 2008 年金融危机的阴影 根据决议基金会的分析，英国的生产力（衡量经济健康状况的重要指标）的增长速度比官方数据显示的更为强劲。该智库表示，财政大臣约翰·希利(John Healey)继承的经济可能终于开始摆脱2008年全球金融危机的长期阴影。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news that UK productivity is growing faster than official figures suggest, potentially emerging from the long shadow of the 2008 financial crisis, offers a moment for reflection. When nations experience renewed economic health, it is easy to attribute success solely to human effort or policy. Yet, this season of potential recovery reminds us to...
reflection.zh: 英国生产力增长速度快于官方数据，可能正在摆脱2008年金融危机的长期阴影，这一消息提供了一个反思的时刻。当一个国家经济复苏时，人们很容易将成功完全归因于人类的努力或政策。然而，这个潜在的复苏季节提醒我们，要承认雅伟是创造财富和促进国家福祉能力的最终来源。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: Government vows to make business rate valuations for pubs and hotels fairer

An independent review for England and Wales will look at improving the system for hospitality venues, which were hit by higher business rate bills this year after the end of pandemic-era relief and when new revaluations took effect. This effort to improve the system before 2029 highlights the ongoing need for integrity and equity in economic governance. Yahweh's word reminds us that just standards are...

title.en: Volodymyr Zelenskyy forced to rule out elections as he faces an enemy from within
title.zh: 泽连斯基被迫排除举行选举的可能性，因其面临内部敌人

summary.en: A former defence minister has urged Ukraine’s leader to hold elections, despite their suspension following Russia’s invasion.
summary.zh: 一位前国防部长敦促乌克兰领导人举行选举，尽管俄罗斯入侵后选举已被暂停。

body.en:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it would be too dangerous for Ukraine to hold an election while fighting Russia, after a call by his former defence minister to organise a vote.

As he fended off the political pressure, Zelenskyy announced a new drone deal with Norway, as European leaders arrived for talks ahead of a meeting on Monday to discuss how to pressure Russia to end its invasion.

Ukraine has suspended elections under martial law, a measure still widely supported by the population as the country focuses on fighting off the Russian invasion launched in 2022.

The Ukrainian leader has previously faced calls both from Russian President Vladimir Putin and United States President Donald Trump to stage a vote, even as Russia rains down missiles and drones across the country on a daily basis.

"I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk," Zelenskyy said during a briefing with journalists on Saturday.

"If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war," he added.

Ukraine has been engulfed in a political crisis over the summer, triggered when Zelenskyy fired popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov . The row forced Zelenskyy to sack his commander-in-chief.

Thousands took to the streets to demand his reinstatement, while Fedorov issued blistering attacks against the army's top brass.

Then, days ago, the ousted Fedorov made a surprise call to find a way to organise elections.

While he did not explicitly state that he wanted to challenge Zelenskyy, the shock move made even some of his supporters distance themselves.

They include how soldiers, millions of Ukrainian refugees and people from occupied territories would cast their ballots, as well as the threat of both interference and physical attacks from Russia.

Only 15 per cent of Ukrainians believe elections should be held before the end of hostilities, according to an opinion poll.

Zelenskyy, despite facing growing domestic criticism as the war drags on, remains largely popular.

Fedorov's team confirmed to Agence France-Presse on Sunday that he plans to visit the US soon — a trip likely to revive speculation about whether he is positioning himself as a rival to Zelenskyy.

The former minister was a prominent backer of the drone warfare strategy that has come to dominate Ukraine's war with Russia, and had pushed for army reforms — winning support among the public.

On Sunday, several European leaders met Zelenskyy in Kyiv for a Nordic-Baltic summit.

Following individual meetings with several leaders, Zelenskyy announced a drone deal with Norway...
body.zh: 总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基周日在公开讲话中表示，在前国防部长呼吁组织投票后，乌克兰在与俄罗斯作战的同时举行选举太危险了。 在顶住政治压力的同时，泽连斯基宣布了与挪威达成的一项新的无人机协议，欧洲领导人在周一的会议之前抵达进行会谈，讨论如何向俄罗斯施压，使其结束入侵。 乌克兰根据戒严令暂停了选举，这一措施仍受到民众的广泛支持，因为该国专注于抵御 2022 年发起的俄罗斯入侵。 这位乌克兰领导人此前曾面临俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普呼吁进行投票的呼吁，尽管莫斯科每天都在全国各地发射导弹和无人机。 泽伦斯基说：“我认为，在这样的战争中，选举本身就是一个巨大的风险。” “现在的选举对于这个国家来说就像一场海啸，将分裂乌克兰。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “如果我们想摧毁这个国家，那么我们可以在战争时期朝着选举的方向前进，”他补充道。 他周六在向包括法新社在内的记者举行的吹风会上发表了上述言论。 今年夏天，乌克兰陷入了一场政治危机，起因是泽连斯基解雇了受欢迎的国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫。这次争吵迫使泽伦斯基解雇了他的总司令。 数千人走上街头要求恢复他的职务，而费多罗夫则对军队高层进行了猛烈攻击。 然后，几天前，被赶下台的费多罗夫突然呼吁寻找组织选举的方法。 虽然他没有明确表示要挑战泽连斯基，但这一令人震惊的举动甚至让他的一些支持者也敬而远之。 其中包括士兵、数百万乌克兰难民和被占领土人民如何投票，以及来自俄罗斯的干涉和人身攻击的威胁。 一项民意调查显示，只有 15% 的乌克兰人认为应该在敌对行动结束之前举行选举。 尽管随着战争的拖延，泽连斯基在国内面临越来越多的批评，但仍然很受欢迎。 费多罗夫的团队周日向法新社证实，他计划很快访问美国，这次访问可能会再次引发人们对他是否将自己定位为泽连斯基竞争对手的猜测。 这位前部长是无人机战战略的重要支持者，该战略已在乌克兰与俄罗斯的战争中占据主导地位，并推动了军队改革，赢得了公众的支持。 周日，几位欧洲领导人在...会见了泽伦斯基。

reflection.en: In times of national crisis, leaders often face immense pressure to make decisions that balance democratic ideals with national survival. President Zelensky's decision to suspend elections in Ukraine, despite internal calls for a vote, highlights the heavy burden of governing authorities who must act for the safety of their people during an ongoing...
reflection.zh: 在国家危机时期，领导人常面临巨大压力，需在民主理想与国家存亡之间取得平衡。泽连斯基总统在乌克兰暂停选举的决定，尽管面临内部举行投票的呼吁，凸显了执政者在持续入侵中为人民安全而行动的沉重负担。罗马书13:1提醒我们，所有执政的权柄都是雅伟所设立的，呼吁我们尊重那些身居领导职位者所做的艰难选择，尤其是在面临存亡威胁之时。

verse.textEn: Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established.
verse.textZh: 在上有权柄的，人人当顺服他，因为没有权柄不是出于神的。

title.en: Trump waves green flag to start IndyCar race through Washington streets
title.zh: 特朗普挥舞绿旗，华盛顿高速印地赛车比赛拉开帷幕

summary.en: The president took a ceremonial lap of the track before the race, which is the culmination of a summer of events to mark the country's 250th birthday.
summary.zh: 总统在比赛前进行了赛道巡游，此次比赛是该国庆祝250周年夏季系列活动的最高潮。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump was among hundreds of people who gathered to see the IndyCar race through the streets of Washington DC on Sunday, marking the culmination of a series of summer events to celebrate the country's 250th birthday.

Ahead of the race, the president and First Lady Melania Trump took a ceremonial lap of the 1.7-mile track in his presidential limousine, The Beast.

As they reached the finish line, Trump's new Air Force One completed a flyover above the capital.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is the first time professional road racing has been hosted in the capital.

With a maximum speed limit of 55mph (89kmh), Washington DC has the lowest speed limit in the United States.

But on Sunday, some of the world's fastest drivers zoomed past the capital's famous monuments and museums at speeds of up to 190mph (306kmh).

The 25 professional drivers competing in the event face 147 laps featuring seven crucial turns, making a total 250-mile course - a nod to the nation's anniversary.

The drivers sped past the Washington Monument and museums on the National Mall, before passing a finish line with the US Capitol building in frame.

Similar to Formula 1, the IndyCar series is a road race featuring open-wheel, single-seater cars.

But unlike F1, where teams design and build their own cars, the engines in IndyCars come exclusively from Chevrolet or Honda.

Organisers of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix say about 140,000 people are expected to attend, with many given free general admission tickets through a lottery.

The event has been a huge logistical and security lift for the city, and has led to widespread road closures, manholes being bolted down, and road resurfacing.

The Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, which primarily runs domestic flights, has been under a three-hour airspace closure to accommodate the US military flyover.

The National Gallery of Art conducted vibration tests to ensure its priceless collection could withstand the powerful rumble of the engines.

On race day, however, the roar of celebration appeared to largely drown out any irritation. Many of those lining the circuit were there after winning tickets through a public lottery. Some wore Uncle Sam hats, while one woman came dressed as the Statue of Liberty. Families had travelled from across the country for what they saw as a once-in-a-lifetime event.

American driver Josef Newgarden told the BBC that the significance of racing through the capital was not lost on him.

"It's super unique. You might never see this again, and as an American driver, it's very special celebrating the 250th anniversary of the country," he said. "It's a beautiful city, and it's very surreal."

In other events earlier this summer, Trump hosted an Ultimate Fighting Championship event on the...
body.zh: 周日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和数百人聚集在华盛顿特区的街道上观看印地赛车比赛，这标志着庆祝美国 250 岁生日的一系列夏季活动达到了高潮。 比赛前，总统和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普乘坐他的总统豪华轿车“野兽”在 1.7 英里长的赛道上绕了一圈。 当他们到达终点线时，特朗普的新空军一号完成了首都上空的飞越。 Freedom 250 大奖赛是第一次在首都举办职业公路赛车比赛。 华盛顿特区的最高限速为 55 英里/小时（89 公里/小时），是美国最低限速的城市。 但周日，一些世界上速度最快的车手以高达 190 英里/小时（306 公里/小时）的速度飞驰过首都著名的纪念碑和博物馆。 参加本次赛事的 25 名职业车手将完成 147 圈比赛，其中包括 7 个关键转弯，赛道总里程为 250 英里——这是对国家周年纪念的致敬。 车手们飞速驶过华盛顿纪念碑和国家广场上的博物馆，然后驶过终点线，画面中是美国国会大厦。 与一级方程式赛车类似，印地赛车系列赛是一项以开轮单座赛车为特色的公路赛。 但与 F1 车队自行设计和制造赛车不同，印地赛车的发动机完全来自雪佛兰或本田。 Freedom 250 大奖赛的组织者表示，预计约有 14 万人参加，其中许多人通过抽奖获得了免费的普通入场券。 此次活动为该市带来了巨大的后勤和安全提升，并导致大范围的道路封闭、沙井被螺栓固定以及道路重铺。 主要运营国内航班的罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场已经关闭了三个小时的空域，以适应美军的飞越。 国家美术馆进行了振动测试，以确保其无价的藏品能够承受发动机的强大隆隆声。 然而，在比赛当天，庆祝的欢呼声似乎基本上淹没了任何恼怒。赛道上的许多人都是通过公共彩票赢得门票后来到现场的。有些人戴着山姆大叔的帽子，而一名女子则打扮成自由女神像。许多家庭从全国各地赶来参加他们认为一生一次的活动。 美国车手约瑟夫·纽加登 (Josef Newgarden) 告诉 BBC，他并没有忽视穿越首都赛车的重要性。 “这非常独特。你可能再也见不到这样的场景了，作为一名美国车手，庆祝这个国家成立 250 周年是非常特别的，”他说。 “这是一座美丽的城市，而且非常超现实。” 在今年夏天早些时候的其他活动中，特朗普在...举办了一场终极格斗锦标赛活动。

reflection.en: The IndyCar race through Washington, D.C., culminating a summer of events for the nation's 250th birthday, highlights human striving and the pursuit of excellence. As President Trump took a ceremonial lap, we are reminded of the temporary nature of even the most celebrated earthly achievements. Yahweh invites us to train for a different kind of prize, an...
reflection.zh: 在华盛顿特区举行的印地赛车比赛，作为该国250周年夏季系列活动的最高潮，彰显了人类的奋斗和对卓越的追求。当特朗普总统进行赛道巡游时，我们被提醒即使是最受赞颂的世俗成就也是暂时的。雅伟邀请我们为一种不同的奖赏而训练，一个超越短暂胜利和国家里程碑的永不朽坏的冠冕。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits' of being US state after trade talks collapse
title.zh: 特朗普称贸易谈判破裂后加拿大想要“成为美国一州的福利”

summary.en: Canada's PM said he was "reluctantly" announcing retaliatory tariffs and accused the US of starting a trade war.
summary.zh: 加拿大总理表示，他“不情愿地”宣布报复性关税，并指责美国发动贸易战。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said Canada wants "the benefits of being a State, without being one" after trade talks between the two countries collapsed late on Friday.

His comments come after negotiations broke down, triggering new 50% US tariffs on a range of Canadian goods, Trump also said American farmers had been charged "massive amounts of Tariffs" for years.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the fresh tariffs a "miscalculation" designed to "hurt and divide us".

Carney confirmed he would match Trump's tariffs "dollar-for-dollar" from 8 September, including levies on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics. The US and Canada are now in a trade "war", he said.

"They asked too much and they offered too little," Carney said on Saturday. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," he added.

Trump's latest comments echo his repeated references to making Canada the "51st state" of America since returning to office, sparking frustration among its leaders and residents.

The collapse of the trade talks upended a deeply integrated trading relationship, with no clear path to resolution.

"We cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked," Carney said.

On Sunday, while speaking to Fox News, Trump said the Canadians were "foolish" to engage in a trade war with the US and think they will "actually win".

Both countries were optimistic of a deal earlier in the week, but talks fell apart after both sides accused the other of making last-minute changes.

The new 50% US tariffs will apply to a range of Canadian goods, in addition to existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber.

They are limited in scope, covering about $20bn (£15bn; C$28bn) of Canadian imports, or about 5% in total, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

The prime minister said Canada was retaliating "reluctantly" to protect its interests. Details of the counter-measures will be released in the coming days, he said.

Leaders of other federal parties in Canada, including the Conservative opposition, voiced support for the prime minister, as have the leaders of some Canadian provinces.

Tariffs - a tax placed on imports from other countries - have been a key component of Trump's trade policy, with the US president arguing they will boost American manufacturing and create jobs at home.

Critics, however, say tariffs have raised prices for American consumers and have disrupted and damaged the global economy.

Carney's speech on Saturday was his first address to Canadians after he announced late on Friday night that a deal would not be reached, accusing the Americans of making "last-minute changes" that were "unfair" and "uneconomic".

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，在两国之间的贸易谈判周五晚间破裂后，加拿大希望“享受作为一个国家而不是一个国家的好处”。 特朗普发表此番言论之前，谈判破裂，引发美国对一系列加拿大商品征收新的 50% 关税，特朗普还表示，美国农民多年来一直被征收“巨额关税”。 加拿大总理马克·卡尼称新关税是“误算”，旨在“伤害和分裂我们”。 卡尼证实，他将从 9 月 8 日起“一刀切”地追平特朗普的关税，包括对钢铁、乳制品、家电和电子产品征税。他说，美国和加拿大现在正处于贸易“战”之中。 “他们要求太多，但提供太少，”卡尼周六表示。 “当你受到攻击时，你就处于战争状态。我们也受到了攻击，”他补充道。 特朗普的最新言论呼应了他重新上任后多次提到的让加拿大成为美国“第51个州”的说法，这引发了加拿大领导人和居民的不满。 贸易谈判的破裂颠覆了深度融合的贸易关系，且没有明确的解决途径。 卡尼说：“我们不能接受他们所提供的东西，我们也不会提供他们所要求的东西。” 周日，特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，加拿大人与美国进行贸易战是“愚蠢的”，并认为他们会“真正获胜”。 本周早些时候，两国都对达成协议持乐观态度，但在双方指责对方在最后一刻做出改变后，谈判破裂。 除了美国对加拿大钢铁、铝、汽车和木材征收的现有关税之外，美国新的 50% 关税还将适用于一系列加拿大商品。 它们的范围有限，涵盖约 200 亿美元（150 亿英镑；280 亿加元）的加拿大进口商品，约占总额的 5%，包括葡萄酒、乳制品、水泥、服装和曲棍球设备。 总理表示，加拿大“不情愿”地进行报复，以保护其利益。他表示，反制措施的细节将在未来几天公布。 加拿大其他联邦政党的领导人，包括保守党反对党，以及加拿大一些省份的领导人都表示支持总理。 关税——对来自其他国家的进口产品征收的税——一直是特朗普贸易政策的关键组成部分，美国总统认为关税将促进美国制造业并在国内创造就业机会。 然而批评者表示，关税提高了美国消费者的价格，扰乱和损害了全球经济。 卡尼周六的讲话是他在周五深夜宣布不会达成协议后首次向加拿大人发表讲话，并指责美国人做出了“不公平”和“不经济”的“最后一刻的改变”。 与此同时，美国谈判代表指责加拿大...

reflection.en: The breakdown of trade talks between the US and Canada, leading to retaliatory tariffs, highlights the difficulty of maintaining peaceful relations between nations. Even when leaders express reluctance, as Canada's Prime Minister did, the path to "live peaceably with all" can be challenging amidst economic disputes. This situation reminds us of the constant...
reflection.zh: 美国和加拿大之间贸易谈判的破裂，以及随之而来的报复性关税，凸显了国家间维持和平关系的难度。即使领导人表达不情愿，如加拿大总理所言，在经济纠纷中“与众人和睦”的道路也充满挑战。这一局面提醒我们，即使与最亲密的邻居，也需要持续努力寻求理解并避免冲突升级。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 30
title.zh: 几内亚垃圾填埋场倒塌造成30人死亡

summary.en: A mound of rubbish at a major waste site buried several homes in the capital, the government says.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 30 people have been killed after a mound of rubbish at a major waste site collapsed on to nearby homes in Guinea's capital Conakry, the government has said.

Another 22 people were injured, including six seriously, in the city's Dar-es-Salam area.

"Significant" resources and personnel - including the military - have been deployed to search for survivors after the collapse at about 02:00 local time following heavy rain overnight, the government added in a statement.

One woman told local media her five children had died in the disaster. There are fears that the death toll will rise further.

Rescuers were later seen using excavators to comb through a mountain of scattered rubbish at the site as local residents gathered nearby.

Guinea's Prime Minister Mamadou Oury Bah visited the scene to assess the situation and oversee the search efforts.

Neighbourhood leader Lancine Sylla had earlier told the AFP news agency he feared there would be a heavy death toll.
body.zh: 几内亚首都科纳克里政府表示，一处主要垃圾场的一堆垃圾倒塌，砸到附近的房屋，造成至少 30 人死亡。 该市达累斯萨拉姆地区另有 22 人受伤，其中 6 人伤势严重。 政府在一份声明中补充说，在连夜大雨之后，当地时间凌晨 02:00 左右发生倒塌事故，包括军队在内的“大量”资源和人员已被部署来搜寻幸存者。 一名妇女告诉当地媒体，她的五个孩子在这场灾难中丧生。人们担心死亡人数会进一步上升。 随后，救援人员使用挖掘机在现场清理堆积如山的垃圾，而当地居民则聚集在附近。 几内亚总理马马杜·乌里·巴前往现场评估局势并监督搜寻工作。 社区领袖兰辛·西拉早些时候告诉法新社，他担心会造成严重死亡人数。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: France links sharp rise in drownings to heatwaves
title.zh: 法国将溺水人数急剧上升与热浪联系起来

summary.en: A government minister says people have been taking risks by going into the water, with 301 deaths since 19 June.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
France has seen 301 drownings since 19 June, a government minister has said, linking the sharp rise in deaths compared to last year to the prolonged heatwaves .

Sports and Youth Minister Marina Ferrari told France Inter radio the number of deaths - a 14% hike on 2025 - was a "tragic toll".

France, Spain and Italy have been hit by heatwaves, which have triggered massive wildfires that scorched thousands of hectares of land.

Ferrari said people have been taking risks by going into the water, adding: "Many deadly accidents have occurred in areas that are not authorised or supervised for swimming."

She said a number of the drownings were recorded in "open water, in canals for example".

Ferrari said the government was working with regional authorities "to improve swimming areas and make things safer".

Speaking on Friday, she added that "many drownings, particularly among the elderly, occurred in individual pools".

The minister said that sudden immersion in cold water on a hot day could cause shock, and in some cases "people can also exceed their physical capabilities".

In June, Ferrari warned that too many people were trying to cool off in rivers and canals without necessarily taking the risks into account.

Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world - but particularly in Europe.

It is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service. , external

The June heatwave saw a nuclear power plant in southwest France temporarily shut down because water temperatures in the River Garonne topped 28C. Under French laws, water used to cool the reactors at the Golfech plant must not exceed that temperature.

Some monuments like the Eiffel Tower also decided to close early because of the high temperatures in Paris during the June heatwave.

The dry conditions also saw wildfires spread across France, with the Gironde, around the city of Bordeaux, in the south-west of the country being the worse affected area, with more than 200,000 people being forced from their homes in late July.

France has logged 7,300 excess deaths between late May and 22 July, according to provisional figures from the public health authorities.

title.en: Could Russia's growing fuel crisis help end the Ukraine war?
title.zh: 俄罗斯日益严重的燃料危机能否有助于结束乌克兰战争？

summary.en: Empty pumps, long waits: Attacks on oil refineries have left Russia increasingly short of fuel. Dissident Russian economists say growing anger about shortages among ordinary Russians could help end the Ukraine war.

body.en:
Empty pumps, long waits: Attacks on oil refineries have left Russia increasingly short of fuel. Dissident Russian economists say growing anger about shortages among ordinary Russians could help end the Ukraine war.

Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries have triggered a new fuel crisis in Russia .

Reuters news agency reports that at least 30 regions are now affected. Unlike the previous wave of shortages, which began in late May and lasted until mid-July, the current crisis is particularly affecting Moscow and the surrounding area, as is apparent from posts on social media. The gas station chains Gazprom Neft and Tatneft have already restricted the sale of fuel in the capital.

"You can't say there isn't any fuel. But it's obvious there's a crisis," says Oleg Grigorenko, editor-in-chief of the Russian independent media portal 7x7 , which Russia has branded a "foreign agent." "It's not just a personal problem if you leave the city and don't know whether you can get back again, for example. It's also an economic problem,"

Grigorenko reports that in several regions taxi drivers, courier services and the construction industry are already losing business, as many of their supply chains are fuel-dependent. "The logistics of private construction companies is heavily reliant on gasoline," Grigorenko explains.

People are also having to queue for hours at gas stations in the southern Russian region of Krasnodar, according to local media. The authorities are blaming this on a supposed increase in demand during the holiday period.

But many locals are saying that this summer season is a disaster. Real estate agent Igor Zakharchenko, from Sochi on the Black Sea coast, wrote on Instagram: "With its quiet atmosphere and leisurely pace of life, Sochi today is reminiscent of the time before the Olympic Games, when there were still not many cars on the roads and the city had far fewer holidaymakers and inhabitants. But the thing is: There's no gas in Sochi."

Speaking on the Russian broadcaster RTVI, Igor Ananskikh, first deputy chairman of the energy committee in the Russian parliament, said he expected the gas supply situation to normalize within two to three weeks.

Economist Nikolai Korzhenevsky says this is unlikely. He left Russia in protest at Moscow's war  against Ukraine and now lives abroad. In an interview with DW, he highlighted the worsening quality of fuel in Russia. Acquaintances had sent him photos of their cars displaying error messages that indicate engine damage caused by impurities in the fuel.

"The car won't start and has to go to the garage. The same people are telling me garages have waitlists of several months, even in Moscow," Korzhenevsky says. "And then you have to wait again for months for replacement parts....

title.en: Ukraine: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections

summary.en: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that holding elections in his country amid the  full-scale Russian invasion would be highly dangerous, in remarks made in response to a call from the former defense minister to organize a vote.

"I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk. Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine," Zelenskyy said in remarks released on Sunday.

Under martial law, elections are currently suspended in the country as it fights the invading Russian forces. The measure has wide public support.

"If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war," Zelenskyy said in the firm rejection of the proposal by former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Fedorov made the call a month after being fired by Zelenskyy as defense minister .

Fedorov enjoys significant support among younger Ukrainians, thousands of whom have been calling for his reinstatement, with some saying he could seek to challenge Zelenskyy if an election did take place.

However, a recent poll showed that Zelenskyy would still be more popular as a presidential candidate.

Zelenskyy was critical of Fedorov in his remarks, saying: "I believe he is going himself — or is being pushed — toward wrong things." 

Zelenskyy also said that Kyiv believed Russia was planning to mobilize 300,000 more troops for its invasion after parliamentary elections take place in September.

He added that Moscow might draft hundreds of thousands more in 2027 as it seeks to capture the rest of Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, one of its main strategic goals.

As Ukraine continues to come under intense missile attacks from its neighbor , Zelenskyy also spoke of having struck an agreement with Germany on the supply of 600 Patriot PAC-2 missile interceptors for 2027-28.

The announcement comes after German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul visited Ukraine on Saturday.

The US Patriots are the only weapon in Kyiv's arsenal that can take on Russia's Iskander-M and Kinzhal ballistic missiles, but ammunition for the system is running short.

As Europe seeks to fill the gap left by a US that, under Donald Trump , has shown ever more reluctance to help Ukraine,  Norway has also said it plans to ‌give ⁠another ⁠85 billion Norwegian ​crowns ($9.2 billion; €7.8 billion) in ​financial ​support ‌to Kyiv in the 2027 ‌fiscal year.

title.en: Faster than Usain Bolt: The five-day robot Olympics putting humanoid autonomy to the test
title.zh: 比尤塞恩·博尔特更快：为期五天的机器人奥运会考验人形机器人的自主性

summary.en: The World Humanoid Robot Games test the limits of technology and innovation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Humanoid robots are racing, lifting, throwing and even playing tennis in Beijing this week, as China puts its rapidly advancing robotics industry through its paces.

The five-day World Humanoid Robot Games bring together more than 50 events, from traditional sports such as the 100m sprint and tug-of-war to challenges modelled on factory floors, restaurants, offices and emergency scenes.

But behind the spectacle and record-breaking times, the real competition is less about how fast a robot can run than how well it can cope when things go wrong.

Organisers are testing whether machines can see, think and respond to the messy unpredictability of the real world, and whether they can eventually perform useful work without a human stepping in.

The games, heavily promoted in Chinese state media, feature 51 events, including 30 sports competitions and 21 scenario-based contests.

More than 40 per cent of the events require robots to operate fully autonomously, according to Huawei, a tech partner of the games.

The event is in its second year, and some robots are already outperforming the 2025 results.

On Saturday, two robots ran faster than Usain Bolt's 9.58-second world record in the 100m sprint. That was a sharp improvement from 2025, when the winning robot's time was more than 20 seconds.

Braking was an issue, as the machines slammed into a thick mat that organisers placed several metres after the finish line.

Another humanoid, the same model as the 100m champion, ran 400 metres in 39.7 seconds, faster than South African Wayde van Niekerk's world record of 43.03 seconds.

"The intensity is higher than last year, which places significant demands on the robot's battery management and thermal dissipation capabilities," said spectator and robotics investor Xu Qiaosheng.

Robots will compete in tug-of-war and weightlifting, while Tai Chi and pitch-pot — in which contestants throw arrow-like sticks into a narrow-necked vase — will give traditional Chinese sports a futuristic twist.

Beyond the spectacle, the more revealing tests could come when robots encounter the small imperfections of the physical world: a cable at the wrong angle, an object just out of reach, a shifting package or a missed step.

That tests whether robots can identify objects, accurately position their hands and bodies, apply controlled force and recover from errors without human intervention.

Lumos Robotics Chief Executive Yu Chao said the games could help improve hardware and provide a showcase for the industry. But Yu said the longer-term value will depend on real-world problem solving.

summary.en: For years, obesity rates in the US have been on the rise, but new data suggests a potential shift. The increasing use of weight-loss medications like Ozempic and Wegovy is being examined for its role in this possible turning point.

body.en:
Obesity rates climbed in the US for years, but now there are signs this could be changing. Use of weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy has increased rapidly — are they helping?

The United States has been grappling with an obesity epidemic since the late 1970s, but there is growing evidence that the constantly climbing obesity rates are beginning to drop.

"We're seeing signs that there's going to be a turning point," said Benjamin Rader, an epidemiologist at Boston Children's Hospital and at Harvard Medical School who conducts research into health trends using large datasets. In 2024, he and his colleagues published a study based on data from more than 16 million adults, which suggested there had been a decline in obesity prevalence in 2023 — for the first time in more than 10 years.

The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey also indicated a slight decline between 2021 and 2023. More recent surveys have also provided evidence of declining figures.

This comes as a series of new drugs, which some people are using for weight loss, have come onto the market. The use of the GLP-1 agonist drugs Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound has increased rapidly in recent years in the US, with prescriptions more than quadrupling between 2021 and early 2026.

Some of the active ingredients in these drugs were originally developed to treat Type 2 diabetes by mimicking a naturally occurring intestinal hormone to promote a feeling of fullness and to slow down gastric emptying. This has led to many patients losing a significant amount of weight.

For Rader, "it seemed like it [the impact of this medicine] was bound to show up in the data" and that it was possible to be "moderately confident that drugs themselves were having an effect."

For Peminda Cabandugama, an endocrinologist and spokesperson for The Obesity Society, which provides support to professionals in the obesity field, "there is strong evidence showing that there is a significant decline in obesity ."

In a written statement to DW, he said the "general opinion is that GLP-1 medications and their combinations and their increased use as well as the recent attention put on the importance of weight management have played a large and direct role in this reduction in obesity prevalence."

But for Rader there is no definitive proof of a causal relationship. He has no doubt that the drugs have led to weight loss in many people at an individual level, but he told DW that it was too soon to say whether it "will lead to a plateau, […] a decrease […] or a slower decrease in the next 20 years" and what the effect on the general population might be.

Cabandugama thinks the current figures might also have been influenced by lifestyle changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic...

title.en: Ukraine: Could ex-defense minister challenge Zelenskyy?
title.zh: 乌克兰：前国防部长能否挑战泽连斯基？

summary.en: Last week, former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video in which he spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. His explosive remarks have sparked widespread public debate.

body.en:
Last week, former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video in which he spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. His explosive remarks have sparked widespread public debate.

This week, Ukraine was rocked by a series of political scandals. A month after stepping down as defense minister, Mykhailo Fedorov addressed the Ukrainian people in a nine-minute speech posted on his YouTube channel.

In his video message, he declares that Ukraine "cannot remain without a fully appointed minister of defense." But, he continues, "the main problem goes much deeper than one position or one ministry."

He says Ukraine's greatest challenge is a "systemic crisis of governance," of which corruption is only a symptom. Fedorov also criticized the fact that no national elections have been held in Ukraine since 2019.

A few hours earlier, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , had proposed Yevhenii Khmara to parliament as the new defense minister. Khmara had been made acting minister of defense on July 20, and parliament confirmed him in the position on August 19.

When Fedorov spoke of corruption in government authorities, he may not have known about the scandal that would break the very day after he published his speech. On August 19, Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators searched the premises of several high-ranking officials, including a presidential deputy chief of staff, Iryna Mudra, and a member of parliament, Vadym Stolar.

Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) stated that it was "conducting a special operation to expose a criminal organization" in conjunction with the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office.

According to the investigating authorities, this organization was led by a current and a former Ukrainian lawmaker, and involved senior officials from the president's office. Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed Mudra from her post as presidential deputy chief of staff the same day.

In his video, Mykhailo Fedorov warns that "it is especially dangerous when society feels that the main criterion for appointing a person is not their professionalism, results, or ability […] but their personal loyalty to the system." He says that a "legal, safe, and realistic mechanism" needs to be found to make it possible to hold elections, even if Russia's war against Ukraine  continues for a long time.

The president dismissed Fedorov from his post as defense minister on July 15. Protests calling for his reinstatement began the following day in Kyiv, Lviv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and other cities. According to polls conducted by the Rating opinion research institute on July 20 and 21, trust in the ex-minister rose from 35% to 65% in the first week of the protests. title.en: What are Trump's options as US eyes 'never been seen' sanctions on Iran?
title.zh: 随着美国考虑对伊朗实施“前所未有”的制裁，特朗普有哪些选择？

summary.en: The head of Iran's supreme national security council has warned that any US action would lead to a confrontation "like an earthquake," as the US considers unprecedented sanctions.

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has vowed to hit Iran hard economically, after treasury secretary Scott Bessent said that Washington would impose measures on Tehran that have "never been seen" as soon as next week.

The United States, ‌the United Nations and the European Union have applied sanctions, implemented trade embargoes and frozen Iranian assets since the late 1970s.

Since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, Washington has levied additional maritime, energy and financial sanctions and started a naval blockade.

Iran — which has withstood decades of punishing sanctions — has denounced US plans to announce new sanctions and on Sunday warned countries against participating in the United States' "economic war" against the country.

Washington has pushed its allies to jump aboard Trump's new campaign to isolate the Iranian economy, as the US president's unpopular war drags toward the six-month mark.

"We declare to all countries ... do not join the economic war waged by the United States," said Mohsen Rezai, the head of Iran's supreme national security council, on Iranian television.

"Any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy."

Data from the US treasury department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) shows the agency has imposed sanctions on more than 1,000 people, vessels and aircraft since Trump began his second term.

Recent measures have targeted Iran's shadow oil fleet; shipping insurers; entities and people enabling Iran's acquisition of weapons; and digital exchanges, freezing an estimated US$500 billion ($697 billion) in Iran-linked cryptocurrency.

Oil shipments are at a virtual standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran threatening to strike any unauthorised oil tankers that try to transit the vital waterway.

Chinese independent refineries known as "teapots" account for a quarter of Chinese refinery capacity. They operate with narrow and sometimes negative profit margins.

China buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. Independent refiners absorb much of this trade, exposing them to so-called secondary measures that penalise entities helping a primary sanctions target.

Past US sanctions have deterred larger independent refiners from buying Iranian oil. But the independent refineries are somewhat immune since they have little exposure to the US financial system, sanctions experts say.

title.en: Canada's Carney stands up to Trump in an escalating trade war. Could his gamble pay off?
title.zh: 加拿大总理卡尼在不断升级的贸易战中奋起反抗特朗普。他的赌博能得到回报吗？

summary.en: Mark Carney was elected last year on a promise to be a tough negotiator with Trump, and remains broadly popular in Canada.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States on Sunday, after walking away from a "bad deal" on trade in a deepening rift between the longtime allies.

Negotiations between the neighbouring countries broke down on Saturday in Washington, triggering new 50 per cent US tariffs that will affect about US$20 billion ($27.9 billion) worth of goods, or 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.

Carney then announced retaliatory duties on US goods, notably steel and dairy products, to take effect on 8 September.

Although Carney stood up to US President Donald Trump by rejecting what he called an "unfair" trade deal, this gamble could prove economically risky.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Canada has been seeking relief from Trump's tariffs on autos, steel and aluminium, which have battered the country's economy, forced job losses and strained what was once an iron-clad trade relationship.

The White House had alleged "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in introducing the duties.

Trump had said Washington "should be able to have a deal with Canada," citing his "good relationship" with Carney.

But on Saturday, Canada's prime minister said Trump set conditions that were ultimately unacceptable even though earlier talks had been positive.

"In recent days, the United States proposed new terms that were uneconomic, unfair and undermined the net benefits for Canada, and called into question the reliability of any deal," Carney said in Ottawa.

"We cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked."

"Our government understood before many that America would transform all of its commercial relationships, that it would put a series of tariffs on its closest allies, and use economic integration as a weapon," Carney said on Saturday.

He pledged that his country would match the US tariffs "dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses".

Carney, the former head of the central banks of Canada and Britain, earned full support across Canada's political spectrum, with opposition leader Pierre Poilievre calling on citizens to "stand united to defend our country against these unfair attacks on our jobs and businesses."

The Globe and Mail, in an editorial, said: "In the end, Prime Minister Mark Carney took the hint from the Canadian public rather than the bait from the US president."

title.en: Kazakhstan's future after the elections: Russia, EU or China
title.zh: 哈萨克斯坦选举后的未来：俄罗斯、欧盟还是中国

summary.en: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections will be followed by the nation continuing its complex geopolitical balancing act between the EU, Russia, and China, amidst ongoing consolidation of presidential power.
summary.zh: 哈萨克斯坦议会选举后，该国总统权力持续巩固，将继续在欧盟、俄罗斯和中国之间进行艰难的平衡。

body.en:
Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.

On August 23, Kazakhstan , a former Soviet country that has recently adopted a new constitution, will hold elections to its parliament.

The legislative body will be transformed from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. Citizens will elect 145 members of parliament via party lists. All seven registered parties have been admitted to the election, including the ruling party, Adilet (which translates to "Justice").

But the election result is the least of the campaign's intrigues. Experts DW interviewed agree that no party other than President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's Adilet stands a chance of winning.

Luca Anceschi, Professor of Eurasian Studies at the University of Glasgow, Scotland, suggests that the new parliament will do the same as the previous one, "which is pretty much to represent whatever the regime wants them to do."

In his view, one should not expect representatives of the genuine opposition to be elected to parliament.

Stefan Meister, Head of the Center for Order and Governance in Eastern Europe, Russia and Central Asia at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), shares this assessment. He says the ruling party is likely to win the election, a scenario also reflected in recent opinion polls. 

Both experts agree that these elections are intended to consolidate Tokayev's power and further weaken the bloc led by   Nursultan Nazarbayev , the country's president from 1991-2019. 

Constitutional amendments approved earlier allow Tokayev to seek another seven-year presidential term in 2029 and replace the two-chamber parliament with a single-chamber assembly called the Kurultai.

According to former Kazakhstani senator Zauresh Battalova, who now heads the NGO Foundation for the Development of Parliamentarism in Kazakhstan, what matters is not the number of chambers in parliament, but "the scope of its powers, its autonomy and its ability to oversee the executive branch of government."

The new constitution has changed not only the structure of parliament but also the way its members are elected. Independent candidates are no longer allowed to run under the current electoral system. Zauresh Battalova sees this as one of the factors limiting voters' political choice.

"The election will be held exclusively on the basis of party lists, in the absence of a political opposition and with limited party competition. The scope for genuine political choice remains extremely narrow," she told DW.

Meister and Anceschi both say that one should not expect any reaction...
body.zh: 权力不断巩固在总统手中的哈萨克斯坦，在周日的议会选举后将不得不继续在欧盟、俄罗斯和中国之间采取强硬的平衡行动。 8月23日，最近通过新宪法的前苏联国家哈萨克斯坦将举行议会选举。 立法机构将从两院制改为单院制。公民将通过政党名单选举 145 名议会成员。所有七个登记政党均已获准参加选举，其中包括执政党 Adilet（意为“正义”）。 但选举结果只是竞选活动中最不重要的一个。德国之声采访的专家一致认为，除了总统托卡耶夫领导的阿迪莱特党之外，没有任何政党有获胜的机会。 苏格兰格拉斯哥大学欧亚研究教授卢卡·安塞斯基表示，新议会将采取与前一届议会相同的做法，“这几乎代表了该政权希望他们做的任何事情。” 他认为，人们不应该指望真正反对派的代表会当选为议会议员。 德国外交关系委员会 (DGAP) 东欧、俄罗斯和中亚秩序与治理中心主任斯特凡·梅斯特 (Stefan Meister) 也同意这一评估。他表示，执政党很可能赢得选举，最近的民意调查也反映了这一情况。 两位专家一致认为，这些选举旨在巩固托卡耶夫的权力，并进一步削弱 1991 年至 2019 年担任该国总统的努尔苏丹·纳扎尔巴耶夫领导的集团。 早些时候批准的宪法修正案允许托卡耶夫在 2029 年寻求另一个七年的总统任期，并用名为“库鲁尔泰”的单院议会取代两院议会。 哈萨克斯坦前参议员、现任哈萨克斯坦议会制发展非政府组织基金会负责人扎乌雷什·巴塔洛娃表示，重要的不是议会的议院数量，而是“议会的权力范围、自治权以及监督政府行政部门的能力”。 新宪法不仅改变了议会的结构，还改变了议员的选举方式。在现行选举制度下，不再允许独立候选人参选。扎雷什·巴塔洛娃认为这是限制选民政治选择的因素之一。 她告诉德国之声：“选举将完全根据政党名单进行，没有政治反对派，政党竞争也有限。真正的政治选择的范围仍然极其狭窄。” 梅斯特和安塞斯基都表示，不应期待任何反应……

reflection.en: As Kazakhstan navigates its complex geopolitical landscape and consolidates presidential power, the need for wise counsel and broad guidance becomes paramount. A nation's stability and well-being are often found not in concentrated power alone, but in the collective wisdom that ensures safety and sound direction.

title.en: Sam was jailed for helping Hong Kong's protesters. He came home to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

"That time was the first time that I was really involved in a social event," said Lau, who’s now 30 and lives in exile in London.

title.en: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record

summary.en: A humanoid robot has set a new 100-meter dash record, completing the distance in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, surpassing Usain Bolt's previous human record.
summary.zh: 在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，一个人形机器人以9.39秒的成绩跑完100米，打破了尤塞恩·博尔特此前保持的人类纪录。

body.en:
A robot has outperformed humans by running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

The humanoid robot, developed by the Beijing Innovation Centre of Humanoid Robotics, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the event.

Eight-time Olympic gold medallist Bolt set the world record for humans in 2009, running 100m in 9.58 seconds.

The robot beat two others including one made by Chinese smartphone maker Honor - which the manufacturer says ran the distance in 9.32 seconds in a test run.

Other events at the robot games, which started on Saturday, include boxing and football, but also household tasks such as folding laundry.
body.zh: 在中国举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，机器人跑得比尤塞恩·博尔特 (Usain Bolt) 保持的 1 亿米短跑世界纪录还要快，从而超越了人类。 由北京仿人机器人创新中心研发的仿人机器人在比赛中跑出了9.39秒的成绩。 八届奥运会金牌得主博尔特在 2009 年以 9.58 秒跑完 100m 的成绩创下了人类世界纪录。 该机器人击败了另外两个机器人，其中包括中国智能手机制造商荣耀制造的一个机器人，该制造商表示，该机器人在测试运行中仅用了 9.32 秒就跑完了距离。 周六开始的机器人比赛的其他项目包括拳击和足球，还有叠衣服等家务活。

reflection.en: The news of a robot surpassing a human athletic record invites us to consider the nature of achievement. While technological advancements are remarkable, the apostle Paul reminds us that earthly crowns are perishable. Our ultimate pursuit is for an eternal crown, found not in fleeting records but in a life lived for Yahweh.
reflection.zh: 机器人打破人类运动纪录的消息，促使我们思考成就的本质。虽然科技进步令人惊叹，但使徒保罗提醒我们，地上的冠冕是会朽坏的。我们最终的追求是那永恒的冠冕，它不在于转瞬即逝的纪录，而在于为雅伟而活的生命。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Chinese robot runs 100m sprint quicker than Usain Bolt’s world record
title.zh: 中国机器人百米冲刺速度超越博尔特世界纪录

summary.en: A new humanoid robot named Lightning has reportedly broken the 100-meter sprint world record, clocking 9.32 seconds in Beijing, surpassing Usain Bolt's human record of 9.58 seconds set 17 years ago.
summary.zh: 据报道，一台名为“闪电”的新型人形机器人，在北京以9.32秒的成绩打破了100米短跑世界纪录，超越了尤塞恩·博尔特17年前创下的9.58秒的人类纪录。

body.en: Lightning the humanoid ⁠robot clocks 9.32sec in Beijing Quicker than ​9.58sec men’s world record set 17 years ago A ⁠robot named Lightning ⁠has run ​the 100m in 9.32 seconds, ⁠beating the human world ⁠record, China’s ​state broadcaster ‌has reported. The humanoid, developed by the Chinese smartphone manufacturer Honor, ‌reached a peak speed of 14.5 metres per second during ‌a test event for ​the second World Humanoid Robot Games, which ⁠began on Saturday. The ​performance surpassed ​the ​9.58sec men’s ​100m world record ​set ​by Usain Bolt 17 years ago at the World Athletics Championships in Berlin. Continue reading...
body.zh: 仿人机器人“闪电”在北京以 9.32 秒的速度跑完，比 17 年前创下的 9.58 秒男子世界纪录还要快据中国国家广播公司报道，一款名为“闪电”的机器人在 9.32 秒内跑完了 100 米，打破了人类世界纪录。这款由中国智能手机制造商荣耀开发的人形机器人在周六开始的第二届世界人形机器人运动会测试赛中达到了每秒 14.5 米的峰值速度。这一成绩超过了尤塞恩·博尔特 17 年前在柏林世界田径锦标赛上创下的 9.58 秒男子 100 米世界纪录。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This remarkable feat by a robot reminds us that earthly achievements, however impressive, are ultimately transient. While we marvel at technological progress, Yahweh invites us to pursue a different kind of prize—one that endures beyond fleeting records and physical limitations.
reflection.zh: 机器人取得的这一非凡成就提醒我们，世上的成就，无论多么令人印象深刻，最终都是短暂的。当我们惊叹于科技进步时，雅伟邀请我们去追求另一种奖赏——一种超越短暂纪录和身体限制的永恒奖赏。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Robot horse and rider steal the spotlight at Chinese conference
title.zh: 机器人马和骑手在中国会议上抢尽风头

summary.en: More than 300 companies are showcasing the latest advances in robotics at a five-day event in Beijing, China, with a robot horse and rider drawing particular attention.
summary.zh: 组织者称，超过300家公司正在中国北京举行的为期五天的活动中展示机器人技术的最新进展，其中一匹机器人马和骑手尤其引人注目。

body.en:
A robot horse and dancing humanoids are among the machines that have been showcased by Chinese manufacturers at a conference in Beijing.

The five-day 2026 World Robot Conference, which started on Wednesday, comes as the country continues to expand its robotics industry.

On the day the conference kicked off, the world's biggest humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics made its stock market debut in Shanghai.

The Chinese firm's machines are competing in the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games, which started on Saturday in the capital. The event involves more than 2,000 robots from 16 countries.
body.zh: 中国制造商在北京举行的一次会议上展示了机器马和跳舞的人形机器人等机器。 为期五天的 2026 年世界机器人大会于周三开幕，正值中国继续扩大机器人产业之际。 大会开幕当天，全球最大的仿人机器人制造商优树机器人在上海上市。 这家中国公司的机器正在参加周六在首都开幕的 2026 年世界人形机器人运动会。此次活动有来自16个国家的2000多台机器人参加。

reflection.en: The dazzling display of robotics at the Beijing conference highlights humanity's remarkable ingenuity and the accelerating pace of technological progress. This rapid increase in knowledge, as observed in Daniel 12:4, invites us to consider the profound implications of our innovations. As we marvel at these advancements, we are reminded to seek wisdom in how...
reflection.zh: 北京会议上机器人技术的精彩展示，彰显了人类非凡的创造力以及科技进步的加速步伐。但以理书12:4所预言的知识的快速增长，邀请我们思考这些创新所带来的深远影响。当我们惊叹于这些进步时，也提醒我们要以智慧来开发和应用这些强大的工具。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Would even an AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima be enough to make humankind protect itself? I fear not | Timothy Garton Ash
title.zh: 蒂莫西·加顿·阿什：即使是广岛规模的人工智能灾难，也足以让人类保护自己吗？我恐怕不会

summary.en: The article expresses concern from Silicon Valley experts that Artificial Intelligence is developing at a pace exceeding humanity's capacity to control it. The author fears that even a catastrophic AI event might not prompt sufficient self-protective measures from humankind.
summary.zh: 文章表达了硅谷专家对人工智能发展速度超出人类控制能力的担忧。作者担心，即使发生一场人工智能灾难，人类可能也无法采取足够的自我保护措施。

body.en: It’s clear here in Silicon Valley that AI is advancing faster than humans’ ability to control it. That means even sober prophecies seem optimistic Here in Silicon Valley, the experts think that within the next couple of years we’ll see an extraordinary takeoff for artificial intelligence. “Welcome to the foothills of the singularity,” as a Stanford University friend greeted me. More prosaically, the imminent breakthrough is described as “recursive self-improvement” – the point at which AI itself trains each successive model of AI, resulting in an exponential development to something which, in many significant respects, is more intelligent than us humans. As Robert Wright puts it in his book The God Test : “Never before has the near-term future … held such a wide array of not-implausible paths for humankind that would be so wildly transformative.” But will this be heaven or hell? Heaven, says Elon Musk, who predicts “an age of amazing abundance” – although he also sees a 10-20% chance of killer robots murdering us all. Hell is more likely according to Geoffrey Hinton , one of the intellectual founding fathers of AI. “My intuition is, we’re toast,” he told an interviewer in 2023. And talking to Sebastian Mallaby , author of The Infinity Machine, a book about the quest for superintelligence, Hinton estimates p(doom) – the probability of human extinction – at 50%, “because I haven’t got a clue how to estimate the real number”. “As soon as evolution [of AI] kicks in, we’re fucked,” he adds cheerfully. But whether it’s God or Godzilla, artificial superintelligence is just around the corner. Timothy Garton Ash is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...
body.zh: 在硅谷，人工智能的发展速度明显快于人类控制它的能力。这意味着即使是清醒的预言也显得乐观。在硅谷，专家们认为，在未来几年内，我们将看到人工智能的非凡腾飞。 “欢迎来到奇点的山麓，”一位斯坦福大学的朋友向我打招呼。更通俗地说，即将到来的突破被描述为“递归自我改进”——人工智能本身训练每个连续的人工智能模型，从而实现指数级发展，在许多重要方面比我们人类更聪明。正如罗伯特·赖特（Robert Wright）在他的《上帝的考验》一书中所说：“在不久的将来……从来没有为人类提供过如此广泛的并非难以置信的道路，并且具有如此巨大的变革性。”但这到底是天堂还是地狱呢？埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 表示，这是天堂，他预测“一个令人惊叹的丰富时代”，尽管他也认为杀手机器人有 10-20% 的可能性谋杀我们所有人。人工智能创始人之一杰弗里·辛顿 (Geoffrey Hinton) 认为，地狱更有可能发生。 “我的直觉是，我们完蛋了，”他在 2023 年对一位采访者说道。在与《无限机器》（一本关于探索超级智能的书）的作者 Sebastian Mallaby 交谈时，Hinton 估计 p(doom)——人类灭绝的概率——为 50%，“因为我不知道如何估计真实的数字”。 “一旦[人工智能]进化开始，我们就完蛋了，”他高兴地补充道。但无论是上帝还是哥斯拉，人工智能都指日可待。蒂莫西·加顿·阿什 (Timothy Garton Ash) 是《卫报》专栏作家继续阅读...

Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that the wise foresee danger and take refuge, while the naive press on and suffer the consequences. As we navigate these complex technological frontiers, may we seek the wisdom to discern potential harms and...
reflection.zh: 正如这篇报道所强调的，人工智能的迅速发展对人类的远见和审慎提出了严峻挑战。箴言27:12提醒我们，通达人预见危险就藏躲，愚蒙人却往前行，自受亏损。在我们探索这些复杂的技术前沿时，愿我们寻求智慧，辨明潜在的危害，并负责任地行动，以保护我们共同的未来。

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 中国正准备执行二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务

summary.en: China is preparing its most ambitious moon mission in two decades, scheduled for next month. The mission aims to explore the lunar surface, specifically searching for water.
summary.zh: 中国正准备在下个月执行其二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务。此次任务旨在探索月球表面，特别是寻找水资源。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

body.zh: 如何探索一个阳光照不到的地方？中国的太空计划很快将启动近年来最具创新性的月球探测任务之一。 近二十年来，我们已经知道月球上存在某种形式的水。我们仍然不知道的是，在永久阴影的陨石坑内到底有多少可接近的水冰，它埋藏的深度有多深，或者它的形式是什么。 我们所知道的是，获取这些水冰将是一个真正的挑战：它是在难以穿越的深坑底部发现的，那里的阳光永远不会照射到，在远低于零下200摄氏度的温度下数十亿年都保持不变。这些是月球上最有价值的地方，但也是最难到达和探索的地方。 自 1959 年 1 月苏联的 Luna-1 探测器到达月球附近以来，月球探索已经取得了长足的进步。阿波罗任务及其后续任务表明，挑战不再仅仅是到达月球。它是为了探索人类和传统漫游车无法轻易到达的地方，并最终确定月球本身是否可以提供未来探险者所需的一些资源。 中国花了二十年的时间制定了一项日益雄心勃勃的月球探测计划，该计划以中国古代月亮女神嫦娥的名字命名。嫦娥七号任务预计将于本月晚些时候飞往我们的天体邻居，尽管最近另一枚中国火箭的失败给发射日期带来了一些不确定性。这就是这个最新任务如此有趣的原因。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 该任务将测试几种月球探索的新方法。它将由轨道飞行器、着陆器、漫游车和漏斗组成。 此外，鹊桥二号月球中继卫星也已就位。它于2024年3月单独发射，随后支持嫦娥六号任务，并将在嫦娥七号任务期间促进地球与月球表面之间的通信。 我们不知道任务将在哪里着陆，但月球南极艾特肯地区靠近沙克尔顿陨石坑的照明山脊上或附近的一个地点是主要候选地点。 漏斗将成为这次任务的真正明星。与轮式漫游车不同，它的设计目的是跳过破碎的地形并下降到阳光永远无法到达的陨石坑中，而传统车辆可能根本无法进入这些地方。 考虑到陡峭的火山口壁、破碎的地形、永久的阴影以及自主导航和通信的需求，将其添加到任务中是有意义的。 中国科学家不会寻找水的迹象；而是寻找水的迹象。我们...

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. body.en:
KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and about 360 employees in the wake of an audit leaks scandal that saw it cut off from new government contracts.

The audit and consulting giant today reported its revenue fell 1% year-on-year, to $2.26bn in the year 2025-26.

While the embattled audit arm had seen revenue grow 11%, its consulting revenue was down 16.9%. Most of the workers to be let go are from the consulting arm.

KPMG’s new chief executive, John Sams , said weak demand for its services was expected to continue beyond the next 12 months, blaming Australia’s weak economy. He said:

The professional services sector is also changing rapidly as client expectations evolve, AI reshapes the way services are delivered and government spending on consultants remains lower. We also recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust …

After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to reduce our workforce and restructure parts of the firm. This is not a decision that has been taken lightly, and we know it will have a very real impact on people.

body.en:
Bird flu has likely spread to a second seal, one day after the first mammal in Australia was confirmed to have contracted the virus.

Five suspected H5 bird flu cases were recorded in South Australia on Monday, including a long-nosed fur seal at The Pages Conservation Park, the state's Department of Primary Industries and Regions said in a statement on Monday morning.

The Pages — which covers two small islands between Kangaroo Island and the mainland — is a haven for the endangered Australian sea lion.

The fur seal has been tested for bird flu, with results expected in the coming days.

The first positive case of the virus in a mammal was confirmed on Sunday in a long-nosed fur seal at Beachport, 300km south of Adelaide, which authorities believed was contracted from wild birds.

Before the new case was announced, Environment Minister Murray Watt said the spread from birds to mammals was inevitable and the government was examining whether further vaccination programs were needed.

"We are likely to see mass mortalities of birds and mammals, and I know that is a very distressing thing for Australians to hear. But we also need to be realistic," he told ABC TV on Monday.

"This is what we've seen happen overseas. Australia is very fortunate that we've been the last continent on Earth to have this strain of bird flu happen. But we are likely to see those kind of events as we have overseas."

Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the federal government was investigating whether bird flu vaccines were available for use in mammals.

"There are trials underway in North America, in California and Hawaii, and this is using a vaccine that's been developed for cattle," she told ABC radio.

"There certainly is nothing commercially available, but we do continue to look at that research."

Bird flu vaccinations have been rolled out to at-risk species, including the little penguins on Victoria's Phillip Island.

Many were corralled into pens to receive the first of two vaccinations on Sunday night.

With case numbers on the rise, authorities have stepped in to do what they can to defend the 5,000-strong colony.

The penguins' nightly ritual of returning to the same burrow, along the same path, made them ideal candidates for vaccination, Phillip Island Nature Parks reserve manager Ben Thomas said.

As a world-first in scale, the process has taken some experimentation and fine-tuning.

"We've had our teams out late into the night for a week now and learning a lot along the process," Thomas said.

body.en:
SBS WorldWatch will soon become a digital-only service, ending its run as a broadcast television channel.

The multilingual news service, which provides news bulletins from international broadcasters, will move entirely to SBS On Demand .

SBS says the shift will allow it to increase the number of bulletins available in most languages.

From 18 September, the channel, which provides international news in 38 languages from 49 broadcasters worldwide, will cease broadcasting and all SBS WorldWatch programming will continue on SBS On Demand.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

As the channel closes, SBS WorldWatch will expand its existing digital service over the coming weeks to include two or more daily bulletins in most languages.

This is more content than could be accommodated on a single linear channel, SBS says, allowing audiences to watch bulletins as soon as they become available rather than waiting for a scheduled broadcast.

SBS On Demand also features two 24-hour FAST channels for English-language news — Euronews and France 24 .

SBS Director of News and Current Affairs, Mandi Wicks, said SBS WorldWatch played an important role in connecting Australians with news and perspectives from around the world, in their preferred language.

"Moving to SBS On Demand gives us the opportunity to build on that service, with more international news bulletins and greater flexibility for audiences to decide when and how they watch," she said.

"We recognise this will be a change for some audiences who are accustomed to watching SBS WorldWatch on linear television. We're committed to supporting them through the transition, while continuing to evolve our services for the future."

SBS is providing multilingual information and guidance through SBS Audio language programs and on SBS WorldWatch channel 35 ahead of the change.

Further information is available here , with additional support available via the SBS Help Centre .

The SBS WorldWatch — News In-Language hub can be found on the SBS On Demand homepage , where audiences can also search for content in their preferred language.

The full SBS On Demand offering features more than 15,000 hours of local and international programming across more than 60 languages, spanning news and current affairs, documentaries, drama, world movies, entertainment, food, children’s content and sport.

This includes dedicated language collections, as well as selected English-language programs with subtitles in Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese.

A Sydney mother has spoken publicly for the first time since surviving a shark attack more than two months ago, crediting community support with helping her "get better, not bitter".

In a post on her GoFundMe donation page, Leah Stewart, 34, said she still had a long way to go, but her recovery had been "remarkable".

"A huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world," she said.

"That means more to me than I can say, and I truly believe it’s played a huge role in my recovery."

Stewart was swimming between the flags close to shore when she was attacked by a great white shark at Coogee Beach on 13 June.
