She was rushed to hospital in a critical condition, being induced in a coma and undergoing multiple surgeries, including the amputation of one of her arms.

The mother of one said she had been focused on her recovery and had "progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this".

"I want you to know that I feel like I’ve been given a second chance at life, and I’m not going to waste it. As I get better, I know I’ll make something of this second chance and aim to give back even more in generosity, care, and love. I will forever be grateful for everything, and everyone, I’ve been given," she said.

Stewart thanked those who had contributed to the fundraiser, which had reached more than $558,000, but it was time to turn donations off.

"What you’ve offered has given us enough to recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road," she said.

Sydney has experienced a spate of shark attacks this year, including three in just 48 hours in January.

On 18 January, 12-year-old Nico Antic was critically injured and later died after being attacked by a suspected bull shark while swimming off rocks in Vaucluse in Sydney Harbour.

The following day, Andre de Ruyter, 27, was attacked while surfing near Manly, suffering extreme blood loss and undergoing surgery to have one of his legs amputated.

An 11-year-old boy's surfboard was also bitten at Dee Why Beach on the same day, but the young surfer escaped injury.

After Stewart was attacked in June, NSW Premier Chris Minns said his government would invest an extra $34 million in drone coverage across NSW beaches.

Should you invest in shares, or property? Is university still worth it, or should you start your own business? With the path to financial security becoming less clear, Insight asks how aspirational people are getting ahead, and whether Australia is a good country to build wealth. Watch Insight episode Gettin' Rich at 8.30PM Tuesday 25 August on SBS or SBS On Demand.

Enosh Tampoe, 23, and his family migrated from Sri Lanka 16 years ago and have been living in the same rental property since then.

The Sydney mortgage and finance adviser says that as an immigrant family "starting from scratch", he felt financially behind his friends at times growing up.

"There were situations where I did feel like [I was] potentially behind — just because at the end of the day, there is that intergenerational wealth ...You'll notice obviously, they have their own houses; they have nice cars ..." he told Insight.

"Having that support from parents — whether it's in the form of getting money or continuing to live at home rent-free and all that stuff — definitely helps."

Feeling he couldn't rely on the "whole natural pathway of doing well in school, getting through uni and [getting] a big boy job" to build wealth, he took a hard approach to saving at an early age and bought a Sydney apartment two years ago.

Now, he's giving himself 10 years to save a $600,000 deposit for a $3 million Sydney home where his whole family can live.

"My end goal is … that great Australian dream: owning my own home, building my family and raising them in a nice neighbourhood," he said.

To reach his goal faster, he lives with his parents and rents out his apartment — taking advantage of the tax benefits of negative gearing to build equity.

Negative gearing refers to a situation where the ongoing costs of an investment exceed the rental income received, and the overall loss can then be claimed as a tax deduction.

But as of 1 July 2027, the federal government will restrict the tax benefits of negative gearing to new residential builds.

Enosh says this new law has reduced his borrowing capacity by "around 20 per cent", putting his plans to buy a second investment property this year on hold.

summary.en: We went looking into Australia's weight-loss drug boom. What we found was a market operating outside the prescription system.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:

For Kansasin Darwan, living in Bajool in central Queensland, the weight-loss injection was supposed to be a solution. Instead, she says, it left her barely able to function.

The 48-year-old says she had gained weight during perimenopause and believed her Australian GP was unlikely to prescribe a weight-management medicine because she did not meet the relevant clinical criteria.

In Australia, GLP-1 weight loss drugs are generally prescribed for chronic weight management in adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or a BMI of 27 to under 30 with at least one weight-related health condition.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

So, while on holiday in her home country of Thailand, Darwan went to a beauty clinic in outer Bangkok and bought an injectable medicine branded as Mounjaro.

Beauty clinics in Thailand are generally supervised by doctors. However, the screening process for GLP-1 use can be less extensive than the assessment typically conducted by GPs in Australia. For example, some customers at beauty clinics may be prescribed GLP-1 drugs even if they do not have diabetes or are within a healthy weight range.

"I couldn't concentrate while driving. I wasn't feeling like myself. I couldn't sleep. Even my children noticed that I was different," she tells SBS Thai.

Eighteen out of every 1,000 Australians, or almost 2 per cent of the population, are now taking GLP-1s regularly, according to a study by scientists at the University of New South Wales (UNSW) published in November 2025.

Darwan's experience offers a glimpse into a fast-growing market for weight-loss injections, where some Australians are seeking access overseas, while others are obtaining medicines through social-media sellers and informal supply channels.

An investigation by SBS Thai found weight-loss medicines being offered without a doctor's prescription in Australian community groups, reports of products entering the country through informal channels, and unapproved peptides being marketed as weight-loss products.

But access to these medicines is not uniformly occurring outside the established medical system. Many Australians obtain weight-loss drugs through registered health professionals and pharmacies.

For consumers navigating this market, the distinction between an approved prescription medicine, an experimental drug and an unapproved product can be difficult to see — with experts and authorities warning that using medicines outside approved pathways can carry serious risks.

title.en: One Nation MP admits the party's true migration target 'isn't too different' from Labor's
title.zh: 一国党议员承认该党真正的移民目标与工党的“没有太大不同”

summary.en: Pauline Hanson has had to intervene after one MP's revised intake figure raised key questions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation's immigration stance is under question after an MP said the party would include an extra 100,000 people annually in its policy — bringing its target total higher than present forecasts under Labor.

Farrer MP David Farley, who clinched Sussan Ley's old seat from the coalition at a by-election, told the ABC Insiders program on Sunday morning that his party had decided to separate a "true NOM", or net overseas migration figure, from certain other categories of migrants.

However, party leader Pauline Hanson was forced to quickly intervene, refuting the claims just hours later on social media. Party policy is to "cut net overseas migration to 130,000".

This contradicts messaging from Farley, who said One Nation's stated policy of getting net overseas migration down to 130,000 excluded people brought in under a Pacific scheme, aged-care nurses and other in-demand skilled workers.

Adding those groups would amount to an additional 100,000 arrivals, bringing the total to 230,000 — 5,000 more than the budget forecast of 225,000 in the coming four years.

"What we're doing is we're focusing on the NOM in its true form, and then we've got these programs that have been available now for over a decade that drive our economy," Farley told Insiders.

"The raw number is not too different, but the reality is, where do we need them?

"We don't need them in the great urban metroplex — we need them out to be productive, working in agriculture, engineering, mining."

The comments come as public debate continues around the optimum level of migration to Australia.

Net overseas migration dropped to 306,000 in 2024-25, brought down from a post-pandemic peak of 538,000 under Liberal-National government policy.

Cabinet minister Chris Bowen said net overseas migration could not just be redefined.

"My overwhelming conclusion was he's pretty comfortable with what the government's doing," Bowen told reporters.

"I'm not sure what campaign One Nation's going to run on migration if they're effectively backing in what the Albanese government is doing."

Opposition immigration spokesman Jonno Duniam said voters were owed a clear explanation of what the party's immigration policy actually is.

"These are not semantic distinctions. They have real consequences for housing, infrastructure, essential services, wages, jobs and the economy," he said.

"For a party that has spent years telling Australians it has all the answers on immigration, One Nation is having extraordinary difficulty answering the most basic question of all: how many migrants would actually come to Australia under its policy."

body.en: Outside a commercial building in Causeway Bay, one of Hong Kong’s busiest shopping districts, a column of people carrying umbrellas and flowers wrapped around the block. For hours, mourners waited in the rain so they could pay their respects to Wang Wang, a stray dog who was killed by five boys in mainland China. People wait in line to lay down flowers for Wang Wang, on July 25, 2026. Photo: James Lee/HKFP. Holding a bouquet of white chrysanthemums, Brian patiently waited his turn to cram into a lift that would bring him to a small Buddhist temple on the 23rd floor. The 26-year-old from Guangzhou crossed the boundary into Hong Kong earlier that day to take part in the procession, which he had heard about from social media. Wang Wang and her three puppies were tortured and killed on June 28 in a village in Jieyang, Guangdong province, by five boys all under 14 years old. Videos of the incident, which have since been scrubbed from Chinese social media platforms, show the boys beating the dogs with sticks and dousing Wang Wang in fuel before setting her on fire. Footage of the horrific killings spread throughout the internet, ending up on social media feeds in Hong Kong and beyond. As billboards funded by ordinary Chinese people went up in New York’s Times Square and around the Taipei 101 skyscraper, Hongkongers have also tried to advocate for animal rights in mainland China. “When I first saw the video I was furious, and now I just feel helpless. I just hope I can send off Wang Wang and her puppies one last time,” said Brian, who used a pseudonym for fear of reprisals. Brian, from Guangzhou, brought chrysanthemums to pay his respects to Wang Wang, on July 25, 2026. Now, mourners would only be allowed to lay down flowers outside the venue. The funeral’s organiser, the Hong Kong Animal Rights Association, also pulled out of an interview with HKFP on the morning of the ceremony. Brian was also unaware that the entrance of the building would be flanked by half a dozen plainclothes police officers. body.en: Chief Secretary Eric Chan said efforts by the current-term government in helping ethnic minorities, such as the setting up of dedicated care teams, have brought "real impact". Speaking at the Carnival of Care and Harmony on Sunday, Chan said two more support service centres were established in 2024, raising the total to 10, with ethnic minority care teams operating at each centre. "Each team is led by a social worker, supported by programme workers and volunteers who are familiar with the languages and cultures of the communities they serve," he said. "In just over two years, these teams have reached some 18,000 ethnic minority households. That is real impact." Looking ahead, the chief secretary said the government will continue its efforts in helping ethnic minorities better integrate into society. Edited by Edmond Fong

title.en: Chinese comedian Guo Degang investigated after patriotic song gag
title.zh: 中国喜剧演员郭德纲因爱国歌曲笑话被调查

summary.en: A famous Chinese comedian is under investigation, local authorities told AFP on Sunday, after he reportedly poked fun at a patriotic song during a performance. The ruling Communist Party maintains tight control over China’s arts scene, and the government has enacted laws in...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自香港栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: A famous Chinese comedian is under investigation, local authorities told AFP on Sunday, after he reportedly poked fun at a patriotic song during a performance. Chinese comedian Guo Degang. Photo: Kai Tak Sports Park. The ruling Communist Party maintains tight control over China’s arts scene, and the government has enacted laws in recent years to protect national heroes and symbols from purported slander. Guo Degang, 53, allegedly improvised part of a 1956 tune about Chinese fighters defeating Japanese soldiers in World War II during a performance in the central city of Wuhan in July, according to local media reports. The Wuhan culture and tourism bureau confirmed by phone to AFP on Sunday that an investigation into Guo was ongoing, but it was not clear what stage it had reached. Guo, from the northern city of Tianjin, is known for reviving a style of rapid comic dialogue called crosstalk — “xiangsheng” in Chinese — during the 2000s and 2010s. He has performed on state broadcaster CCTV’s annual Spring Festival Gala and at the Great Hall of the People, a grand government building in Beijing that hosts major state events. Guo was unable to be reached on social media, and his Weibo account seems to have been inactive since August 9. The Great Hall of People in China. Photo: Mirko Kuzmanovic, via Shutterstock. Venues in other Chinese cities have postponed perfomances featuring Guo this month and have been offering refunds. The song, “Playing My Beloved Pipa”, was recognised in 2019 as an “outstanding” song celebrating the founding of The People’s Republic of China, online outlet The Paper reported this month. In one instance, Guo allegedly changed the lyric, “quiet on Weishan Lake”, to “quiet in the Forbidden City” — China’s former seat of imperial power — and performed the lines with a “comedic” touch, the report said. Authorities had not approved his riff before the performance, The Paper said, citing Wuhan’s culture bureau. It reported that local authorities were investigating Guo for “suspected violations” of rules on commercial performances. Under President Xi Jinping, authorities have tightened their oversight of arts performances, including comedy shows. In 2023, authorities fined a performing group the equivalent of millions of dollars and suspended their shows indefinitely after a comic made an oblique joke about the armed forces. Li Haoshi referenced a well-known army slogan while joking about watching his dogs chase a squirrel — which officials said had “caused a bad social impact” and broken the law.
body.zh: 地方当局周日告诉法新社，一名中国著名喜剧演员正在接受调查，据报道他在表演中取笑一首爱国歌曲。中国喜剧演员郭德纲。照片：启德体育公园。执政的共产党对中国的艺术界保持着严格的控制，政府近年来颁布了法律来保护民族英雄和象征免受所谓的诽谤。据当地媒体报道，53 岁的郭德纲据称在 7 月在中部城市武汉的一场演出中即兴创作了一首 1956 年的歌曲，该歌曲讲述的是二战中中国战士击败日本士兵的故事。武汉文化和旅游局周日通过电话向法新社证实，对郭的调查正在进行中，但尚不清楚调查进展到什么阶段。郭来自北方城市天津，因复兴 2000 年代和 2010 年代一种名为相声的快速相声风格而闻名。他曾在中央电视台一年一度的春节联欢晚会上以及在人民大会堂（北京一座举办重大国家活动的宏伟政府大楼）进行表演。无法在社交媒体上联系到郭，他的微博账户似乎自 8 月 9 日以来一直处于闲置状态。 中国人民大会堂。照片：Mirko Kuzmanovic，来自 Shutterstock。中国其他城市的场馆已推迟本月郭的演出并提供退款。据澎湃新闻本月报道，这首歌曲《弹奏我心爱的琵琶》被评为2019年庆祝中华人民共和国成立“优秀”歌曲。报道称，有一次，郭据称将歌词“微山湖静”改为“紫禁城静”——中国以前的皇权所在地——并以一种“喜剧”的方式表演台词。澎湃新闻援引武汉市文化局的消息称，当局在演出前并未批准他的即兴表演。据报道，地方当局正在调查郭“涉嫌违反”商业演出规则。在习近平主席的领导下，当局加强了对包括喜剧表演在内的艺术表演的监管。 2023 年，一名喜剧演员对武装部队开了一个拐弯抹角的玩笑，当局对一个表演团体处以数百万美元的罚款，并无限期暂停他们的演出。李浩石一边开玩笑说自己看着自己的狗追松鼠，一边引用了一句著名的军队口号——官员们表示，这“造成了恶劣的社会影响”，而且触犯了法律。

title.en: China mulls bid to host 2028 UN climate talks: sources
title.zh: 中国考虑申办2028年联合国气候谈判：消息人士

summary.en: China is mulling a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028, two sources familiar with the matter told AFP Friday, as it seeks to burnish its reputation as a leader in the fight against global warming. Beijing has not yet made a final decision regarding the proposal for the COP33...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自香港栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: China is mulling a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028, two sources familiar with the matter told AFP Friday, as it seeks to burnish its reputation as a leader in the fight against global warming. The United Nations in Geneva, Switzerland. Photo: Wikicommons. Beijing has not yet made a final decision regarding the proposal for the COP33 summit, both sources said, nor is there a clear timeline for doing so. The host does not have to be decided this year. China’s interest was first reported by Bloomberg News. The UN’s annual climate gatherings rotate among regional blocs. This year’s COP31 is scheduled to take place in Turkey, followed by COP32 in Ethiopia in 2027. The 2028 summit falls to the Asia-Pacific. In April, India withdrew its offer to host COP33 without specifying a reason. South Korea has previously expressed interest. The Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a query for comment. The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) secretariat told AFP: “We have not been informed by the Asia-Pacific Regional Group on the nomination of the host country for COP33. “Regional groups hold consultations first to determine which country from their respective regions will offer to host on behalf of the group. Once agreed, the chair of that regional group formally sends an official nomination to the secretariat.” China has in recent years positioned itself as a counterweight to the United States. The White House. Photo: White House, via Flickr. Under President Donald Trump, the US left the landmark Paris climate agreement twice while the administration seeks to boost fossil fuels. Hosting UN climate talks could thus be an opportunity for China to boost its credentials as a climate leader. The world’s second-largest economy also has an economic interest as the leading exporter of green technologies, including solar panels, electric vehicles, wind turbines and batteries. US-China dynamics But hosting the gathering could also cast an unwelcome spotlight on China, which, with its population of 1.4 billion and massive manufacturing industry, is the world’s biggest greenhouse emitter, followed by the United States, India and the European Union. Although it has pledged to achieve carbon neutrality before 2060, it is targeting only a modest 7-10 percent reduction in economy-wide greenhouse gas emissions by 2035, compared to peak levels. Another piece that China is considering is the US-China dynamic, one source said. Climate cooperation had been a key feature of the bilateral relationship under former presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, and COP33 could spur renewed collaboration if a Democrat is elected in 2028. The summit would likely fall days after the US presidential election...
body.zh: 两名知情人士周五告诉法新社，中国正在考虑申办 2028 年联合国气候谈判，以提升其作为应对全球变暖领导者的声誉。联合国位于瑞士日内瓦。照片：维基共享资源。两位消息人士称，北京尚未就 COP33 峰会的提议做出最终决定，也没有明确的时间表。今年不必决定主办方。彭博新闻社最先报道了中国的兴趣。联合国年度气候会议在区域集团之间轮流举行。今年的 COP31 定于土耳其举行，COP32 将于 2027 年在埃塞俄比亚举行。2028 年峰会将在亚太地区举行。 4月份，印度撤回了主办COP33的提议，但没有具体说明原因。韩国此前曾表达过兴趣。中国驻华盛顿大使馆没有立即回应置评请求。联合国气候变化框架公约（UNFCCC）秘书处告诉法新社：“我们尚未收到亚太区域集团关于COP33主办国提名的通知。区域集团首先进行磋商，以确定各自地区的哪个国家将代表该集团主办。”一旦达成一致，该区域组主席将正式向秘书处发送正式提名。”近年来，中国将自己定位为制衡美国的力量。白宫。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。在唐纳德·特朗普总统的领导下，美国两次退出具有里程碑意义的巴黎气候协议，而政府则寻求增加化石燃料。因此，主办联合国气候谈判可能成为中国提升其气候领导者地位的机会。作为世界第二大经济体，作为太阳能电池板、电动汽车、风力涡轮机和电池等绿色技术的主要出口国，也拥有经济利益。美中动态 但主办这次聚会也可能会让人们不受欢迎地把注意力集中在中国身上。中国拥有 14 亿人口和庞大的制造业，是世界上最大的温室气体排放国，其次是美国、印度和欧盟。尽管它承诺在 2060 年之前实现碳中和，但其目标只是到 2035 年将整个经济的温室气体排放量比峰值水平小幅减少 7-10%。一位消息人士称，中国正在考虑的另一件事是美中动态。气候合作一直是前总统乔·拜登和巴拉克·奥巴马领导下双边关系的一个关键特征，如果民主党在 2028 年当选，COP33 可能会激发新的合作。峰会可能会在美国总统大选几天后举行……

body.en:
KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and about 360 employees in the wake of an audit leaks scandal that saw it cut off from new government contracts.

The audit and consulting giant today reported its revenue fell 1% year-on-year, to $2.26bn in the year 2025-26.

While the embattled audit arm had seen revenue grow 11%, its consulting revenue was down 16.9%. Most of the workers to be let go are from the consulting arm.

KPMG’s new chief executive, John Sams , said weak demand for its services was expected to continue beyond the next 12 months, blaming Australia’s weak economy. He said:

The professional services sector is also changing rapidly as client expectations evolve, AI reshapes the way services are delivered and government spending on consultants remains lower. We also recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust …

After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to reduce our workforce and restructure parts of the firm. This is not a decision that has been taken lightly, and we know it will have a very real impact on people.

The firm said it was discussing further cuts to a small number of award-based jobs. Sams said KPMG would continue to assess its operating environment as it sought to stay financially sustainable. You can read about the firm’s difficulties here:

title.en: Could teaching assistants be an overlooked teacher pipeline? New research says yes
title.zh: 助教能否成为被忽视的教师输送渠道？新研究称答案是肯定的

summary.en: New research from UNC-Chapel Hill indicates that teaching assistants are a significant and effective source for recruiting and retaining teachers. The study found that nearly one in five new teachers in North Carolina previously worked as teaching assistants and perform comparably to other early-career educators.
summary.zh: 北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的最新研究表明，助教是招聘和留住教师的一个重要且有效的来源。这项研究发现，北卡罗来纳州近五分之一的新教师曾担任助教，并且他们的表现与其他早期职业教师相当。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

As school districts continue searching for ways to recruit and retain teachers, new research from UNC-Chapel Hill suggests one promising pipeline may already be in classrooms: teaching assistants.

A new statewide study from the Education Policy Initiative at Carolina (EPIC) found that nearly 1 in 5 beginning teachers in North Carolina previously worked as teaching assistants.

Researchers also found that these former TAs perform just as well as other early-career teachers—and are significantly more likely to remain in the profession through their second and third years.

The findings also suggest the TA-to-teacher pipeline could help address other workforce needs. Former TAs are more likely to be teachers of color and to hold special education licenses, strengthening areas where many districts face persistent shortages.

Kevin C. Bastian et al, Pathways and Outcomes for Early-Career Teachers With Teaching Assistant Experience, Educational Policy (2026). DOI: 10.1177/08959048261461454

title.en: Collaborative drawing offers new insights into how strangers become friends
title.zh: 协作绘画为陌生人如何成为朋友提供了新的见解

summary.en: The closer two people grow, the more alike their brains work—or so the assumption goes. Two ETH Zurich studies challenge this idea by examining the brain activity of younger and older adults who drew together over several weeks. Despite growing closer, the similarity of their...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

The closer two people grow, the more alike their brains work—or so the assumption goes. Two ETH Zurich studies challenge this idea by examining the brain activity of younger and older adults who drew together over several weeks. Despite growing closer, the similarity of their brain activity did not simply increase.

What happens in the brain when two people engage in joint creative activity and build a new relationship with one another in the process? ETH cognitive scientist Ryssa Moffat investigated this question. She is a postdoctoral researcher at the Social Brain Sciences Lab within the Chair of Cognitive and Social Neuroscience.

Her study has now been published in the journal PLOS Biology . The setting was as follows: Over a period of six weeks, 61 pairs met six times to draw together. The participants came from a younger age group (18 to 35 years) and an older age group (70 to 85 years) and were divided into 31 cross-generational pairs and 30 pairs of the same age.

At the outset, the participants did not know each other and first had to become familiar with one another. At each session, the pairs first drew individually on separate sheets of paper, then drew together twice on a single sheet of paper. They were free to decide whether to take turns or draw simultaneously. They were allowed to converse throughout the session but were instructed to remain silent while drawing.

At each session, the researchers recorded participants' brain activity with wearable brain sensors. This enabled the researchers to investigate how the process of getting to know one another was reflected in the pairs' brain activity. At the same time, the mobile sensors ensured that participants could move and respond to each other naturally, as in everyday life, without distorting the recorded signals.

The similarity of brain activity was particularly crucial for the ETH researchers: To what extent do the brains of two people synchronize during an encounter? And how does this synchronization change over the course of repeated sessions? The focus was not on whether a pattern of brain activity corresponds to a specific subjective feeling such as liking or irritation.

Moffat was interested in what researchers call " inter-brain synchrony ": When people perform a shared task such as drawing, each person's brain reacts continuously to the other person's actions—and the brains can be said to be "synchronized" when similar changes in brain activity occur simultaneously in both people.

body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 两个人的关系越亲密，他们的大脑就越相似——至少是这样的假设。苏黎世联邦理工学院的两项研究通过检查几周内聚集在一起的年轻人和老年人的大脑活动来挑战这一观点。尽管越来越接近，但他们大脑活动的相似性并没有简单地增加。 当两个人进行共同的创造性活动并在此过程中彼此建立一种新的关系时，大脑会发生什么？ ETH 认知科学家 Ryssa Moffat 研究了这个问题。她是社会脑科学实验室的博士后研究员，担任认知和社会神经科学系主任。 她的研究现已发表在《PLOS Biology》杂志上。设定如下：在六周的时间里，61对组合进行了六次碰头抽奖。参与者来自较年轻的年龄组（18至35岁）和较年长的年龄组（70至85岁），并分为31对跨代和30对同龄。 一开始，参与者互不相识，首先要互相熟悉。在每次训练中，两人首先在不同的纸上单独画画，然后在一张纸上一起画两次。他们可以自由决定是轮流画还是同时画。他们被允许在整个会议期间交谈，但被要求在绘画时保持沉默。 在每次会议中，研究人员都用可穿戴大脑传感器记录参与者的大脑活动。这使得研究人员能够调查彼此了解的过程如何反映在两人的大脑活动中。同时，移动传感器确保参与者可以像日常生活一样自然地移动和相互响应，而不会扭曲记录的信号。 大脑活动的相似性对于苏黎世联邦理工学院的研究人员来说尤其重要：两个人的大脑在相遇时的同步程度如何？在重复会话的过程中，这种同步会如何变化？重点不在于大脑活动模式是否对应于特定的主观感觉，例如喜欢或刺激。 莫法特对研究人员所说的“脑间同步”很感兴趣：当人们执行绘画等共同任务时，每个人的大脑都会对另一个人的动作做出持续的反应——当两个人的大脑活动同时发生类似的变化时，可以说大脑是“同步的”。 先前关于大脑间同步的研究表明，两个大脑的活动模式变得越来越......

title.en: France links sharp rise in drownings to heatwaves
title.zh: 法国将溺水人数急剧上升与热浪联系起来

summary.en: A government minister says people have been taking risks by going into the water, with 301 deaths since 19 June.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
France has seen 301 drownings since 19 June, a government minister has said, linking the sharp rise in deaths compared to last year to the prolonged heatwaves .

Sports and Youth Minister Marina Ferrari told France Inter radio the number of deaths - a 14% hike on 2025 - was a "tragic toll".

France, Spain and Italy have been hit by heatwaves, which have triggered massive wildfires that scorched thousands of hectares of land.

Ferrari said people have been taking risks by going into the water, adding: "Many deadly accidents have occurred in areas that are not authorised or supervised for swimming."

She said a number of the drownings were recorded in "open water, in canals for example".

Ferrari said the government was working with regional authorities "to improve swimming areas and make things safer".

Speaking on Friday, she added that "many drownings, particularly among the elderly, occurred in individual pools".

The minister said that sudden immersion in cold water on a hot day could cause shock, and in some cases "people can also exceed their physical capabilities".

In June, Ferrari warned that too many people were trying to cool off in rivers and canals without necessarily taking the risks into account.

Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world - but particularly in Europe.

It is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service. , external

The June heatwave saw a nuclear power plant in southwest France temporarily shut down because water temperatures in the River Garonne topped 28C. Under French laws, water used to cool the reactors at the Golfech plant must not exceed that temperature.

Some monuments like the Eiffel Tower also decided to close early because of the high temperatures in Paris during the June heatwave.

The dry conditions also saw wildfires spread across France, with the Gironde, around the city of Bordeaux, in the south-west of the country being the worse affected area, with more than 200,000 people being forced from their homes in late July.

France has logged 7,300 excess deaths between late May and 22 July, according to provisional figures from the public health authorities.
body.zh: 一位政府部长表示，自 6 月 19 日以来，法国已发生 301 起溺水事件，死亡人数较去年大幅上升与持续的热浪有关。 体育和青年部长玛丽娜·法拉利 (Marina Ferrari) 告诉法国国际米兰电台，死亡人数比 2025 年增加 14%，这是一个“悲惨的数字”。 法国、西班牙和意大利遭受热浪袭击，引发大规模野火，烧毁了数千公顷土地。 法拉利表示，人们一直在冒险下水，并补充道：“许多致命事故发生在未经授权或监管的游泳区域。” 她说，许多溺水事件是在“开放水域，例如运河”中发生的。 法拉利表示，政府正在与地方当局合作“改善游泳区并使事情变得更安全”。 她在周五发表讲话时补充说，“许多溺水事件，特别是老年人溺水事件，都发生在个别泳池中”。 这位部长表示，在炎热的天气里突然浸入冷水可能会导致休克，并且在某些情况下“人们还会超出其身体承受能力”。 六月，法拉利警告说，太多人试图在河流和运河中降温，而没有考虑到风险。 气候变化正在推高世界各地的气温，尤其是在欧洲。 根据哥白尼气候服务机构的数据，它是变暖最快的大陆，升温速度是全球平均水平的两倍。 , 外部 6月的热浪导致法国西南部的一座核电站暂时关闭，因为加龙河的水温高达28摄氏度。根据法国法律，用于冷却戈尔菲什核电站反应堆的水不得超过该温度。 由于六月热浪期间巴黎的高温，埃菲尔铁塔等一些古迹也决定提前关闭。 干燥的气候还导致野火蔓延至法国各地，其中该国西南部波尔多市周围的吉伦特省受灾最严重，7月下旬已有超过20万人被迫离开家园。 根据公共卫生当局的临时数据，5月下旬至7月22日期间，法国已有7,300人超额死亡。

body.en: Researchers have uncovered a possible reason why the Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 can disrupt the brain long before memory problems begin. In mice, APOE4 increased a protein called Nell2, shrinking neurons and making memory circuits unusually active. That early hyperactivity predicted worse memory later in life. Reducing Nell2 in adult mice reversed the abnormal changes, raising hopes for a new way to intervene before Alzheimer’s progresses.

body.en: Researchers at CERN have created microscopic versions of the early Universe by colliding surprisingly small atomic nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The collisions produced quark-gluon plasma, the ultra-hot matter believed to have filled the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Even more intriguingly, the particles left behind reveal the shape of the nuclei that created them, offering a new way to probe both nuclear physics and the Universe’s earliest moments.

title.en: How a new era of heatwaves could shake up the school calendar
title.zh: 新时代的热浪如何改变学校日历

summary.en: Teachers warn it could be increasingly difficult for classrooms to function during the hottest months.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Over the past two weeks, the sound of children has returned to Scotland's school playgrounds. Their summer breaks began in late June or early July and ended in mid-August.

In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, however, children will not return until early September. Their holidays are a similar length to Scotland's but England and Wales schools did not break up until late July, something that meant pupils were in school during the peak of the early summer heat.

Or at least they were meant to be in school. While it was 30C or more outside, inside many classrooms it felt far hotter. With no air conditioning and limited ventilation, the heat became stifling and more than 1,000 schools across the UK either closed or sent pupils home early before the hottest part of the afternoon. Conditions were particularly challenging for GCSE and A‑level students sitting exams during extreme heat.

Baroness Brown, chair of the UK's Climate Change Adaptation committee, has warned that "we know high temperatures can significantly impair concentration and performance" of children in schools.

Back in February 2026, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said the timing of the school holidays should be reconsidered: "It's pretty hot usually in May, June and July, just at the point you're asking children to sit down and take an exam… so I think there is a need to have a good old look at it [the school year]."

The recent hot weather has seen some parents join his call. Andrea Bigger, a parent in London, is "absolutely aware of the dangers" of extreme heat in classrooms. She says her daughter has previously suffered from heat exhaustion and was hospitalised after overheating at her primary school. She is "really concerned that the UK is not ready or prepared for this".

And this summer was not a one off. BBC analysis of temperature data shows a clear shift. In the 1960s, the first 30C day was occurring on average on 13 July. In the 2020s that figure has been 19 June.

So, is it going to be increasingly difficult for schools to operate in the summer months? And is moving the school summer holidays the solution to ensuring pupils are able to be taught for as much of the year as possible?

This summer is likely to become the hottest on record, according to the Met Office. Multiple temperature records have been broken with five widespread heatwaves and four consecutive months where the temperature has exceeded 35C. This has never happened before.

June saw one of the UK's most intense heatwaves, with up to seven consecutive days where temperatures were well above the official heatwave thresholds of 25-28C - just as the exam period was in full swing. Temperature records were broken too: 38C was recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June, the hottest June day ever measured...
body.zh: 过去两周，孩子们的声音又回到了苏格兰的学校操场。他们的暑假从六月底或七月初开始，到八月中旬结束。 然而，在英格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰，孩子们要到九月初才能返回。他们的假期长度与苏格兰相似，但英格兰和威尔士的学校直到七月下旬才放学，这意味着学生们在初夏最热的时候仍在上学。 或者至少他们本来应该在学校里。虽然室外温度高达 30 摄氏度或更高，但许多教室内却感觉更热。由于没有空调且通风有限，炎热天气变得令人窒息，英国各地 1000 多所学校要么关闭，要么在下午最热的时候提前让学生回家。对于在酷暑期间参加考试的 GCSE 和 A-level 学生来说，条件尤其具有挑战性。 英国气候变化适应委员会主席布朗男爵夫人警告说，“我们知道高温会严重影响学校儿童的注意力和表现”。 早在 2026 年 2 月，Ofsted 的首席督察马丁·奥利弗爵士就表示应该重新考虑学校放假的时间：“通常五月、六月和七月天气非常热，就在你要求孩子们坐下来参加考试的时候……所以我认为有必要重新审视一下[学年]。” 最近天气炎热，一些家长也加入了他的呼吁。伦敦的一位家长安德里亚·比格（Andrea Bigger）“完全意识到”教室里酷热的危险。她说，她的女儿此前曾出现过中暑症状，在小学时因中暑而入院治疗。她“真的担心英国还没有为此做好准备”。 今年夏天并不是一次性的。 BBC 对温度数据的分析显示出明显的转变。在 20 世纪 60 年代，第一个 30 摄氏度的天气平均出现在 7 月 13 日。在 2020 年代，这个数字是 6 月 19 日。 那么，学校在夏季的运营会变得越来越困难吗？推迟学校暑假是否是确保学生能够在一年中尽可能多的时间接受教育的解决方案？ 据英国气象局称，今年夏天可能会成为有记录以来最热的夏天。连续4个月气温超过35摄氏度，连续4个月打破了多项气温记录。这以前从未发生过。 6 月是英国最强烈的热浪之一，连续 7 天的气温远高于官方热浪阈值 25-28 摄氏度，而考试期间正是如此。气温记录也被打破：6 月 26 日，诺福克郡林伍德记录了 38 摄氏度，这是有史以来最热的 6 月一天……

body.en:
A county in Wales had one of the world's highest carbon emissions per square kilometre due to wildfires in July, according to a charity.

The fire above Blaenavon, Torfaen was described as "one of the largest and most challenging" in south Wales in recent years by the fire service.

Save the Children said it was concerned about possible health consequences after data , external published by the European Union's earth observation programme, Copernicus, showed Torfaen behind Malanje in Angola, Spain's Ávila and Annaba in Algeria in terms of wildfire emissions in July.

Torfaen council said it was unaware of the EU data but its own air quality monitoring showed "elevated particulate concentrations".

A blaze the size of about 300 football pitches broke out on Mynydd Garnclochdy, between Abersychan and Blaenavon, with people reporting smelling smoke about 30 (48km) miles away in Cardiff.

Combined with others across the region it contributed to a major incident being declared , which eventually required assistance from the military .

Blaenavon councillor Janet Jones said the smoke had been "particularly bad" on 13 August - about three weeks after the fire first ignited.

"There was great concern about air quality and the impact on elderly people and those suffering with respiratory issues such as emphysema and COPD."

Jones said she had spoken with GP practice nurses two weeks ago and was not aware of any increase in patients complaining about respiratory problems, but added this "could change in the months ahead".

Melanie Simmonds, head of Save the Children Wales, said: "In Wales and across the world, children are breathing in smoke from wildfires, coping with extreme heat and losing the freedom to play outdoors because the air is no longer safe.

"These conditions are not only frightening - they carry serious health consequences for children whose bodies and lungs are still developing."

Torfaen council said it was not aware of the research and "it is not clear what data or evidence was used in the assessment to arrive at the reported conclusion".

It said it "recognises that prolonged wildfire incidents have the potential to adversely affect local air quality, particularly through increased levels of smoke and particulate matter".

It added it "continuously monitors" air quality through a monitoring station in Croesyceiliog Cwmbran.

"While elevated particulate concentrations have been observed during the wildfire period, the council's monitoring station is intended to provide information on general background air quality rather than conditions at specific locations immediately adjacent to the fires," it said.

body.en:
As parents across the country prepare to wave their children off to university, conversations about family finances and the cost of living are growing ever more frequent - and fervent.

Yet every year, millions of pounds worth of scholarships and bursary funding goes unclaimed by students - with many unaware the extra help exists.

So roll up the next generation of gamers, who this year can apply for as esports scholarship from the University of Roehampton - with more than 100 handed out so far.

But can the students balance their studies and their esports? And is the scholarship set to catch on?

It is different from standard video gaming as esports includes spectators, much like traditional sports.

Gamers compete against one another in high-stakes tournaments for cash prizes and trophies.

Roehampton is offering esports scholarships to undergraduate and postgraduate students who show that they can balance academic progress and video-gaming excellence.

"This scholarship is about recognising talent in a field that has a growing popularity both around the world and among our students," University of Roehampton registrar Mark Ellul said.

Scholars are expected to compete in weekly university tournaments as well as representing the university at in-person events.

Roehampton requires minimum rankings in major games for the scholarship, but will consider applications from those close to the threshold who meet other criteria, such as having large followings on streaming platforms like Twitch.

Former esports scholar Cameron Dray found out about Roehampton through the esports scholarship. Inspired by similar initiatives at American universities, he looked into whether anything similar was on offer in the UK.

Initially, the university was offering just £1,500, but due to the team's performance and rise in popularity, the amount was raised to £2,000.

"This money was crucial to me as it gave me the opportunity to study in a very expensive city without the need for part-time work," Dray said.

"There were requirements that came alongside the scholarship, but none that were unexpected or not transparent when applying," he added.

Dray encouraged students to make use of every scholarship, bursary and opportunity available to them.

He said: "Many of these funds are available to more students than they realise, and everyone should be taking full advantage."

The average graduate in England leaves university with debts of more than £47,500 . Scholarships such as Roehampton's can reduce student debt and provide additional financial support.

body.zh: 随着全国各地的父母准备让孩子上大学，有关家庭财务和生活成本的讨论变得越来越频繁和热烈。 然而，每年都有价值数百万英镑的奖学金和助学金无人领取——许多人不知道还有额外的帮助。 因此，请聚集下一代游戏玩家，他们今年可以申请罗汉普顿大学的电子竞技奖学金——迄今为止已发放了 100 多名奖学金。 但学生们能否平衡学业和电子竞技呢？奖学金会流行吗？ 它与标准视频游戏不同，因为电子竞技包括观众，就像传统体育运动一样。 玩家在高风险锦标赛中相互竞争，争夺现金奖励和奖杯。 罗汉普顿正在为本科生和研究生提供电子竞技奖学金，这些学生表明自己能够平衡学业进步和视频游戏的卓越表现。 罗汉普顿大学教务长马克·埃鲁尔 (Mark Ellul) 表示：“这项奖学金旨在表彰这个在世界各地和我们的学生中越来越受欢迎的领域的人才。” 学者们将参加每周举行的大学锦标赛，并代表大学参加现场活动。 罗汉普顿要求获得奖学金的主要游戏的最低排名，但会考虑那些接近门槛且满足其他标准的申请，例如在 Twitch 等流媒体平台上拥有大量粉丝。 前电子竞技学者卡梅伦·德雷 (Cameron Dray) 通过电子竞技奖学金了解了罗汉普顿。受到美国大学类似举措的启发，他研究了英国是否也有类似的举措。 最初，该大学只提供 1,500 英镑，但由于球队的表现和知名度的上升，金额提高到 2,000 英镑。 “这笔钱对我来说至关重要，因为它让我有机会在一个非常昂贵的城市学习，而不需要兼职工作，”德雷说。 他补充说：“奖学金附带有一些要求，但申请时没有一个是意外的或不透明的。” 德雷鼓励学生利用一切可用的奖学金、助学金和机会。 他说：“其中许多资金提供给比他们意识到的更多的学生，每个人都应该充分利用。” 英国大学毕业生平均背负超过 47,500 英镑的债务。罗汉普顿奖学金等奖学金可以减少学生债务并提供额外的财务支持。 托马斯·科尔（Thomas Cole）是一位绰号为“Pac”的电子竞技运动员，专攻赛车游戏《赛道狂飙》（Trackmania），他表示，大学提供包括电子竞技在内的独特奖学金，通过降低...的水平来鼓励学生在学术上的发展。

body.en: China's "Manned Space" program issued a terse announcement on Sunday regarding its much-anticipated Chang’e 7 lunar exploration mission. The agency stated: "In keeping with the principle of proceeding prudently and reliably, and ensuring absolute success, after a comprehensive assessment it has been determined that the Chang’e 7 mission does not meet the conditions for launch and therefore cannot be carried out during the planned launch window this year." The Chinese message offered no explanation for the cause of the delay from the Wenchang Space Launch Site, located on an island in the South China Sea. Consisting of a lunar orbiter, lander, rover, and a mini-hopper of a probe, the mission was due to launch as early as Sunday on a Long March 5 rocket. It is intended to land at the South Pole of the Moon. Read full article Comments

title.en: Volcanoes that made history
title.zh: 创造历史的火山

summary.en: Enormous eruptions altered Earth’s climate and societies all over the globe.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: The first telegram arrived in Singapore on a Monday, sent from the city of Batavia in the Dutch East Indies (now Jakarta, Indonesia). “Terrific detonations from Krakatau (volcanic island),” it reported. Soon afterward: “Stones falling. Village near Anjer washed away.” The wires continued clattering out news of bridges destroyed, boats smashed, lighthouses “disappeared.” By noon on Tuesday, the scope of the natural disaster was clear: “Where once Mount Krakatau stood the sea now plays.” Within days, the source of the destruction was known worldwide. On the morning of August 27, 1883, a volcanic eruption had obliterated two islands in the strait between Java and Sumatra, and most of a third. More than 36,000 people perished, the majority in devastating tsunamis that raced outward from the colossal explosion. Thanks to Victorian-era telecommunications, it was the first time in history that people around the globe could begin to document, in near real time, the immediate and long-term effects of a catastrophic volcanic eruption. What they learned over the next few years laid the foundations for the modern science of volcanology. And it was an especially eye-opening lesson in how the biggest eruptions can influence climate, agriculture, and even the course of human history. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 第一份电报于周一抵达新加坡，是从荷属东印度群岛的巴达维亚市（现印度尼西亚雅加达）发出的。报道称，“喀拉喀托（火山岛）发生了可怕的爆炸。”不久之后：“石头落下。安杰尔附近的村庄被冲走了。”电线继续发出有关桥梁被毁、船只被撞、灯塔“消失”的消息。到周二中午，自然灾害的范围已经很清楚了：“喀拉喀托山曾经矗立的地方现在变成了大海。”几天之内，破坏的根源就被全世界所知。 1883 年 8 月 27 日早晨，火山喷发摧毁了爪哇和苏门答腊之间海峡的两个岛屿，以及第三个岛屿的大部分。超过 36,000 人丧生，其中大部分死于巨大爆炸引发的毁灭性海啸。得益于维多利亚时代的电信技术，这是历史上第一次，世界各地的人们可以开始近乎实时地记录灾难性火山喷发的直接和长期影响。他们在接下来几年中学到的知识为现代火山学科学奠定了基础。这是一次特别令人大开眼界的教训，让我们了解到最大规模的火山喷发如何影响气候、农业，甚至人类历史的进程。阅读全文 评论

title.en: Putting mice into hibernation causes a major loss of synapses
title.zh: 让小鼠冬眠会导致突触大量丧失

summary.en: Hibernation cuts down on synapses, but mice seem to retain memories anyway.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Our leading hypothesis for how our memories are stored is that when you learn something, the connections among neurons involved get stronger and physically larger, and that constitutes the memory. The trouble is that these connections significantly change over time—they’re plastic. “If you compare the arrangement of these connections on day one with the same on day four or five, it's very, very different," says Kazumasa Tanaka, a neuroscientist at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University in Japan. To learn how a memory that can last for years can sit on hardware that shifts every few days, Tanaka’s team made the shift a bit more dramatic. In a recent Science study, they induced a hibernation-like state in mice, which basically erased the state of more than half of their synapses. And yet the mice apparently have kept their memories. Hibernation on demand Hibernation is a specialty of squirrels, hamsters, and bears, but the neural circuit that triggers it is conserved across mammals, and is present in species that never hibernate in the wild—like mice. In June 2020, a team of researchers led by Takeshi Sakurai, a neuroscientist at the University of Tsukuba and a collaborator on Tanaka’s study, developed a technique to artificially activate this hibernation circuit. This can be done by activating a population called Q neurons in a region of the hypothalamus. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 关于我们的记忆如何存储，我们的主要假设是，当你学习某些东西时，相关神经元之间的连接会变得更强，物理上也会变得更大，这就构成了记忆。问题在于这些连接会随着时间的推移而发生显着变化——它们是塑料的。日本冲绳科学技术研究生院的神经科学家 Kazumasa Tanaka 表示：“如果你将第一天的这些连接的排列与第四天或第五天的相同排列进行比较，就会发现这是非常非常不同的。”为了了解如何将可以持续数年的内存放置在每隔几天变化一次的硬件上，田中的团队让这种变化变得更加戏剧化。在最近的一项《科学研究》中，他们在小鼠中诱导了类似冬眠的状态，这基本上消除了它们一半以上突触的状态。然而老鼠显然保留了它们的记忆。按需冬眠 冬眠是松鼠、仓鼠和熊的特长，但触发冬眠的神经回路在哺乳动物中是保守的，并且存在于在野外从不冬眠的物种（如小鼠）中。 2020 年 6 月，由筑波大学神经科学家、田中研究合作者樱井武 (Takeshi Sakurai) 领导的研究小组开发了一种人工激活这一冬眠回路的技术。这可以通过激活下丘脑区域中称为 Q 神经元的群体来完成。阅读全文 评论

title.en: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
title.zh: TikTok 将向美国支付 4 亿美元，这是最大的儿童隐私和解协议之一

summary.en: The deal stems from a 2024 lawsuit alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
TikTok has agreed to pay $400m (£293m) to the US to end a lawsuit alleging its platform violated children‘s privacy, marking one of the largest ever settlements over the issue.

The deal stems from a 2024 suit by the Department of Justice under former President Joe Biden alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.

Doing so was against the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), a federal law enacted in 2000. It is the same law that dozens of US states are now suing Meta over .

"Children and parents are better protected today than they were when this case began," assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said.

Other companies to have paid penalties to the US government for COPPA violations include Google's YouTube, which in 2019 paid $170m, and Epic Games, which in 2022 paid $275m.

Meta is also now facing penalties that could exceed hundreds of billions of dollars stemming from COPPA violations alleged by attorneys general of 29 US states. A jury trial in the lawsuit started this week , with the Instagram and Facebook owner accused of targeting child users and profiting from them.

While the TikTok lawsuit predates last year's split of TikTok's US business and operations from its original base of China, the settlement only involves TikTok's operations in China.

ByteDance, which is a privately held company, was most recently valued by investors at $550bn , external .

Under the terms of the deal, TikTok and ByteDance will immediately pay the DOJ $300m. It will pay another $100m when the government vacates a 2019 consent decree , external with the Federal Trade Commission.

As part of the agreement, the predecessor to ByteDance, Musical.ly, was required to pay a $5.7m fine for COPPA violations and ensure it sought parental consent for any user aged under 13.

The justice department did not detail on Friday any action against TikTok beyond the fine. But the department noted that since it sued the platform, TikTok has "undergone significant changes," including to its ownership, privacy practices and platform controls for young users.

When the lawsuit was filed, attorneys for the US said there were more than 170 million teenagers using TikTok and that the app was "directed to children." Yet, it did not effectively gauge the age of users or get parental consent for use from those underage.

In 2024, former President Biden pushed for TikTok to be either banned, or have the company divest its US operations. President Donald Trump went on to support divestment of the app, which occurred last year.

Its US operations are now 81% owned by a consortium of investors, while Bytedance maintains a 19% stake.
body.zh: TikTok 同意向美国支付 4 亿美元（2.93 亿英镑），以结束指控其平台侵犯儿童隐私的诉讼，这是该问题有史以来最大的和解协议之一。 该交易源于前总统乔·拜登领导下的司法部于 2024 年提起的诉讼，指控 TikTok 及其母公司字节跳动收集了数百万 13 岁以下用户的“大量数据”。 这样做违反了 2000 年颁布的联邦法律《儿童在线隐私保护法》(COPPA)。美国数十个州现在正在通过同一法律起诉 Meta。 助理司法部长布雷特·舒马特说：“与此案开始时相比，今天的儿童和家长得到了更好的保护。” 其他因违反 COPPA 行为而向美国政府支付罚款的公司包括谷歌旗下的 YouTube（2019 年支付了 1.7 亿美元）和 Epic Games（2022 年支付了 2.75 亿美元）。 美国 29 个州总检察长指控 Meta 因违反 COPPA 规定而面临可能超过数千亿美元的处罚。该诉讼的陪审团审判于本周开始，Instagram 和 Facebook 所有者被指控针对儿童用户并从中获利。 虽然 TikTok 诉讼早于去年 TikTok 的美国业务和业务从其原来的中国基地剥离出来，但和解协议仅涉及 TikTok 在中国的业务。 字节跳动是一家私营公司，最近投资者的外部估值为 5500 亿美元。 根据交易条款，TikTok 和字节跳动将立即向司法部支付 3 亿美元。当政府撤销 2019 年联邦贸易委员会的同意令时，它将再支付 1 亿美元。 作为协议的一部分，字节跳动的前身 Musical.ly 需要因违反 COPPA 规定而支付 570 万美元的罚款，并确保其为所有 13 岁以下的用户征求家长的同意。 周五，除了罚款之外，司法部没有详细说明针对 TikTok 采取的任何行动。但该部门指出，自起诉该平台以来，TikTok“经历了重大变化”，包括其所有权、隐私做法和对年轻用户的平台控制。 提起诉讼时，美国律师表示，有超过 1.7 亿青少年使用 TikTok，并且该应用程序“针对儿童”。然而，它并没有有效地衡量用户的年龄，也没有获得未成年人使用的父母同意。 2024 年，前总统拜登推动禁止 TikTok，或者让该公司剥离其美国业务。唐纳德·特朗普总统继续支持去年撤资该应用程序。 其美国业务目前由一个投资者财团持有 81% 的股份，而字节跳动则保留 19% 的股份。

title.en: How landscape gardening is being electrified
title.zh: 园林景观如何电气化

summary.en: The switch to quieter electric equipment is not going as fast as some would like.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Part of the soundtrack to a day in southern California is the drone of petrol-powered gardening equipment.

Noise is one of the main reasons that cities around the US , external are banning petrol landscaping tools or encouraging electric alternatives.

These alternatives have the additional benefits of reducing carbon emissions, vibrations and the exposure of landscapers to pollution.

In addition they can mean longer working hours, as they can be used at times when residents demand quiet.

Today, I'm taking part in training run by the American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA), an organisation supporting the transition towards electric landscaping equipment.

To my surprise, the electric backpack leaf blower I strap on is not much heavier than my normal rucksack. Using the blower to herd balls around the park feels fairly intuitive, though naturally I'm much clumsier and slower than the pro landscapers.

As for noise, there's still a buzz, but the sound is higher-pitched and not quite so loud as the familiar petrol-powered machines.

The move to electric power is attracting new companies to the market for gardening kit.

US aerospace start-up Whisper Aero is one of those firms. Its main business is electric propulsion systems for aircraft.

But in 2022, after the Covid-19 pandemic made many people more sensitive to noise, and following a couple of years of research and development, the company realised that its aerospace-grade fans would work well in leaf blowers.

"Our technology is cleaner, quieter and more efficient than other air-moving technologies that exist today," according to Andrew Terajewicz, Whisper Aero's director of air management. "And the leaf blower is the perfect mix of this."

The company has had to scale up its manufacturing volume in its expansion to consumer technology.

Online pre-orders of Whisper Aero's handheld leaf blower started this year. It's priced at the high-end of electric leaf blowers, which are often more expensive than traditional petrol versions.

"It is so ultra quiet yet powerful, that the brain has a hard time understanding what's happening," says Dan Mabe, the former landscaper who founded AGZA.

Whisper Aero aims to further develop its products, including a backpack leaf blower that would be better suited to professional landscapers.

Even with innovation like that, petrol-powered machines are unlikely to disappear anytime soon, particularly for professional landscapers.

For a start, petrol machines are much more powerful, which makes for quicker work, so less time is spent lugging around heavy equipment.

Terajewicz says that heavy-duty petrol backpack blowers can reach a maximum blowing force of about 50 newtons.
